requirements.title: Claude session refuses to start when no executable is resolved
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:83 - guard let executable = configuration.executable else { throw ProviderError.notInstalled(configuration.provider) }
requirements.preconditions: A thread on provider .claude; ProviderRegistry could not resolve an executable so SessionConfiguration.executable is nil.
requirements.expected_result: start() throws ProviderError.notInstalled(.claude) before any process is spawned. Its errorDescription is exactly "Claude is not installed. Install it and sign in with `claude auth login`." (the backticks are part of the string).
failure_cases: This IS the failure path; no further work is done.
requirements.windows_path: Executable resolution is the platform boundary (PA-0010): the bare name "claude" must resolve through PATH plus PATHEXT, where an npm install typically leaves claude.cmd rather than an extensionless file. A failure to resolve must reach this same throw, not a spawn error.
requirements.verification_method: unit test on the session factory with a nil executable, asserting the exact message

requirements.title: Claude session id is the resume id, else a fresh lowercased UUID
requirements.preconditions: start() has passed the executable guard.
requirements.expected_result: id = configuration.resumeID when non-nil (an EMPTY STRING is not treated as nil here, unlike Command Code and Pi), otherwise UUID().uuidString.lowercased(), a lowercase hyphenated UUID. start() returns this id on success.
requirements.persistence: The returned id becomes the thread's provider resume id, stored by the thread runtime, not by this file.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: UUID generation is platform neutral; the lowercasing must be invariant (ASCII), not locale sensitive.
requirements.verification_method: unit test asserting lowercase form and resume passthrough

requirements.title: Claude session base argument vector is exactly 14 tokens in a fixed order
requirements.expected_result: The array begins with exactly these 14 tokens in this order: "-p", "--input-format", "stream-json", "--output-format", "stream-json", "--verbose", "--include-partial-messages", "--permission-prompt-tool", "stdio", "--setting-sources", "user,project,local", "--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions", "--permission-mode", <permissionMode>. "user,project,local" is ONE token with no spaces.
side_effects: These tokens become the spawned command line
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: Tokens are passed as an argv array to CreateProcess with MSVCRT quoting; no shell is involved in the source and none may be introduced.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture capturing the spawned argv, compared token for token

requirements.action: modeName is computed at init, on every send, and after an approved ExitPlanMode.
requirements.expected_result: interaction == .plan returns "plan" and is tested FIRST, overriding the runtime mode. Otherwise: .supervised -> "default", .autoAcceptEdits -> "acceptEdits", .auto -> "auto", .fullAccess -> "bypassPermissions". These five strings are verbatim, camelCase where shown.
failure_cases: none - the switch is exhaustive over RuntimeMode
requirements.windows_path: Pure function, no platform boundary.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over all 8 combinations of four runtime modes and two interaction modes

requirements.title: Claude appends --effort only for a non-empty effort, with no known-effort check

requirements.title: Claude fast mode passes --settings with a literal JSON token
requirements.expected_result: Two tokens are appended: "--settings" and the single token {"fastMode":true} - exactly 18 characters, no spaces, no escaping, double quotes around fastMode only.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: The token contains double quotes. Windows argv quoting must deliver it byte-identically; naive quoting that strips or doubles the quotes breaks the CLI's parse.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture asserting the token as received inside the child process

requirements.title: Claude MCP config passes three tokens under one condition, or none at all
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:94-96 - comment plus if let mcpConfig = MCPProviderConfig.claudeConfigPath() { arguments += ["--mcp-config", mcpConfig, "--strict-mcp-config"] }
DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPProviderConfig.swift:212-215 - claudeConfigPath() returns MCPPaths.claudeConfigURL.path only when serversPresent(in:key:"mcpServers")
requirements.preconditions: MCP settings have produced a claude config file with a non-empty mcpServers object, or have not.
requirements.expected_result: When claudeConfigPath() returns a path, THREE tokens are appended together: "--mcp-config", the path, "--strict-mcp-config". When it returns nil, NEITHER flag is passed and Claude reads the user's own MCP configuration as usual. The two flags are one unit and never appear apart.
side_effects: The CLI reads the named config file
failure_cases: Missing or empty config file: both flags omitted; this is not an error.
requirements.windows_path: The path contains backslashes and may contain spaces; it is one argv token and must not be split.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture with and without a connected MCP server

requirements.title: Claude probes --help once per executable path for two optional flags and does not cache a failed probe
requirements.action: start() asks for the executable's known options.
requirements.expected_result: On a cache hit keyed by executable.path the cached Set is returned and no process runs. On a miss, Shell.run(executable, ["--help"], environment: environment, timeout: 20) runs; ANSI is stripped from result.output + result.errorOutput; the Set is the members of the literal two-element array ["--system-prompt-snapshot", "--forward-subagent-text"] whose text appears in the help output; that Set is cached. If Shell.run throws, the EMPTY set is returned and NOTHING is cached, so the next launch probes again.
side_effects: One `claude --help` child process per executable path, bounded at 20 seconds
requirements.persistence: In-memory static cache for the life of the app process only; nothing on disk.
failure_cases: Probe throws or times out: empty set, not cached, both optional flags omitted for that launch. Behaviour can therefore differ between the first and second launch after a probe failure.
requirements.cancellation: Governed only by Shell.run's 20 second timeout.
requirements.windows_path: Shell.run maps to the Windows process layer (PA-0007, PA-0008). ANSI stripping is load-bearing on Windows because CLIs emit VT sequences into pipes.
requirements.verification_method: unit test with a scripted stand-in emitting help text, then a failing stand-in, asserting the second launch probes again

requirements.title: Claude passes --system-prompt-snapshot off when the help probe found the flag
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:99-100 - comment "Resumed chats must use the current setting, even with Hydra off." then if options.contains("--system-prompt-snapshot") { arguments += ["--system-prompt-snapshot", "off"] }
requirements.expected_result: Two tokens appended: "--system-prompt-snapshot" then the literal "off". Appended for every session, Hydra on or off. Omitted entirely when the probe did not find the flag.
failure_cases: A failed probe omits the flag (PR-PROVCLI-009).
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture

requirements.title: Claude with natively-run Hydra passes --agents with the compact agent JSON as one token
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:102-108 - if let hydra = configuration.hydra { if hydra.runsNatively { arguments += ["--agents", HydraPrompts.claudeAgents(hydra).compactString] ... } }
requirements.expected_result: Two tokens appended: "--agents" then HydraPrompts.claudeAgents(hydra).compactString, the whitespace-free JSON serialization as ONE argv token.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: A large JSON token with embedded double quotes on one command line. CreateProcess caps the command line at 32767 characters; a long agent definition plus --append-system-prompt can approach it. The port must measure the real ceiling against the largest Hydra configuration rather than assume it fits.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture plus a long-agent stress case

requirements.action: start() sets hydraPolicy and evaluates the forwarding flag.
requirements.expected_result: hydraPolicy is set to HydraPrompts.policy(for: .claude, hydra). Exactly ONE token "--forward-subagent-text" is appended, and only when the help probe found it; it takes no value.

requirements.title: Claude caps concurrent subagents through an environment variable, not an argument
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:111-112 - comment "Uncapped, the CLI keeps its own limit on heads at once." then if let cap = hydra.maxHeads { environment["CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS"] = String(cap) }
requirements.preconditions: Hydra on, runs natively, hydra.maxHeads non-nil.
requirements.expected_result: The spawned process environment gets CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS with the decimal string of the cap. When maxHeads is nil the key is NOT written and NOT cleared. This is the ONLY environment key ClaudeSession writes; everything else is configuration.environment unchanged.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: Windows environment variable names are case-insensitive; the key must still be written with this exact casing, and the environment block must be constructed explicitly rather than inherited implicitly.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture reading the child's environment

requirements.title: Claude with Hydra heads on another provider disallows Agent and Task as two bare tokens
requirements.action: start() builds the fallback Hydra block.
requirements.expected_result: hydraPolicy becomes HydraPrompts.fallbackPolicy(hydra), and THREE tokens are appended: "--disallowedTools", "Agent", "Task" - one flag followed by two separate bare positional values, NOT one comma-joined value. This is an upstream oddity and is reproduced exactly.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: Three separate argv elements; quoting must not merge them.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture asserting three distinct argv elements
requirements.upstream_defect: provider-argv-and-handshakes.md section 10 item 2 (Claude --disallowedTools emits two bare positionals after one flag)

requirements.title: Claude always passes --append-system-prompt, even with an empty value
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:121-128 - comment "Exactly one combined system prompt segment for every session, Hydra or not." then arguments += ["--append-system-prompt", [hydraPolicy, AntiSlopPolicy.instructions(enabled: configuration.antiSlopEnabled)].compactMap { $0 }.joined(separator: "\n\n")]
requirements.action: start() appends the combined system prompt.
requirements.expected_result: Two tokens are appended UNCONDITIONALLY: "--append-system-prompt" then the joined text. The value is [hydraPolicy, AntiSlopPolicy.instructions(enabled:)] with nils removed, joined by exactly two newline characters. With Hydra off and anti-slop off both are nil and the second token is the EMPTY STRING; the flag is still passed. Its position is after the Hydra flags and before the resume tail.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: An empty argv token must survive Windows quoting as an empty argument (a bare pair of double quotes), not be dropped. This is the likeliest Windows regression in this vector.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture asserting the child receives an empty argument in that position
requirements.upstream_defect: provider-argv-and-handshakes.md section 10 item 1 (--append-system-prompt passed with an empty value)

requirements.title: Claude's resume tail is mutually exclusive: --resume plus optional anchor, or --session-id
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:129-134 - if let resumeID { arguments += ["--resume", resumeID]; if let anchor = configuration.resumeAt { arguments += ["--resume-session-at", anchor] } } else { arguments += ["--session-id", id] }
requirements.expected_result: With a resume id: "--resume" then the id, then, ONLY if configuration.resumeAt is non-nil, "--resume-session-at" then the anchor. Without a resume id: "--session-id" then the generated id. --session-id and --resume never appear together; --resume-session-at never appears without --resume.

requirements.title: Claude spawns one line-framed process per thread in the thread's working directory and attaches a reader
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:136-151 - StdioProcess(executable:arguments:directory:environment:), try process.start(), readTask iterating process.messages then didClose()
requirements.expected_result: One StdioProcess is created with the executable, the argument array, directory = configuration.workingDirectory and the built environment, with the DEFAULT framing (newline-delimited JSON, not Content-Length). try process.start() propagates a launch failure out of start(). A read Task then consumes process.messages one JSON object at a time calling handle(_:), and calls didClose() when the stream ends. isRunning reports the process's own isRunning.
side_effects: One child process for the life of the thread session
failure_cases: process.start() throwing propagates out of start() unchanged.
requirements.windows_path: The lines framer must split on 0x0A only and tolerate a trailing 0x0D reaching the JSON parser, because the source does not strip CR (port_impacts.md entry 18). The child must be placed in a Job Object so its own children die with it (PA-0007).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test against the scripted Claude stand-in in tests/fixtures

requirements.title: Claude sends an initialize control request as its first message, with two extra fields under native Hydra
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:154-160 - var initialize: [String: JSONValue] = ["subtype": "initialize", "hooks": .null]; if configuration.hydra?.runsNatively == true { initialize["agentProgressSummaries"] = true; initialize["forwardSubagentText"] = true }; let initialization = try await control(.object(initialize))
requirements.expected_result: The request object is {"subtype":"initialize","hooks":null}. Under native Hydra ONLY, two boolean fields are added: "agentProgressSummaries": true and "forwardSubagentText": true. It is sent through control(_:) and start() awaits its response. A thrown control error propagates out of start().
side_effects: One line written to the child's stdin
failure_cases: A control_response with subtype "error" throws ProviderError.failed with its error string, or "Claude rejected the request." when absent.
The process closing first throws the stored launch error (PR-PROVCLI-061).
requirements.windows_path: None beyond the framing.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture comparing the emitted JSON line byte for byte

requirements.title: Claude control requests are numbered droppy-code-<n> from 1 and resolved by exact id match
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:301-310 - control(_:) pre-increments controlCounter, builds requestID = "droppy-code-\(controlCounter)", stores the continuation and sends {"type":"control_request","request_id":<id>,"request":<request>}
requirements.action: Any control request is made (initialize, set_permission_mode, set_model, interrupt, stop_task).
requirements.expected_result: controlCounter is incremented BEFORE use, so the first request id is exactly "droppy-code-1". The literal prefix is "droppy-code-". The wire object is {"type":"control_request","request_id":"droppy-code-<n>","request":<the request object>}. The reply is matched on message.response.request_id and resolves that continuation. control() throws ProviderError.notRunning when there is no process, and ProviderError.failed(launchError ?? "Claude exited.") when hasClosed is already true.
failure_cases: hasClosed already true: throws with the stored launch error or the verbatim "Claude exited."
No process: ProviderError.notRunning, described as "The agent session is not running."
requirements.cancellation: didClose resumes every waiting continuation by throwing.
requirements.windows_path: None. The id prefix is a contract with the app's own reader (port_impacts.md entry 20) and must not be renamed with the product.
requirements.verification_method: unit test on the counter plus a contract fixture on the envelope

requirements.title: Claude publishes the model catalog carried in the initialize response
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:161-163 - isStarted = true; let models = Self.models(in: initialization); if !models.isEmpty { onEvent?(.models(models, current: configuration.model)) }

Entries without a string value are skipped. A non-empty list is emitted as .models(list, current: configuration.model); an empty list emits nothing.

A non-empty result emits .commands(list); an empty result emits nothing. Unlike the static catalog probe (PR-PROVCLI-026), a MISSING commands array here is not an error.

requirements.title: Claude's static catalog probe uses a 9-token argv that is not a subset of the session argv
requirements.preconditions: A resolved executable and a directory to probe.
requirements.action: ProviderRegistry asks Claude for its catalog and commands.
requirements.expected_result: A bare StdioProcess is spawned with exactly those 9 tokens in that order. Measured against the session argv it OMITS four things (--include-partial-messages; --permission-prompt-tool stdio; --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions; --permission-mode <mode>) and ADDS one (--no-session-persistence) positioned after --verbose and before --setting-sources. None of the conditional session arguments appear, because the array is a literal that is never appended to.
side_effects: One short-lived child process per catalog refresh
failure_cases: See PR-PROVCLI-026 and PR-PROVCLI-027.
requirements.windows_path: Using the session argv here would hang the probe on --permission-prompt-tool stdio and leave a session file behind on every catalog refresh (port_impacts.md entry 5).
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture capturing the probe argv token for token

requirements.title: Claude's catalog probe terminates the process after 20 seconds and again on every exit path
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:193-197 - watchdog Task sleeping 20 seconds then process.terminate() if not cancelled; defer { watchdog.cancel(); process.terminate() }
requirements.expected_result: A detached Task sleeps exactly 20 seconds and, if not cancelled, terminates the process. A defer cancels the watchdog and terminates the process AGAIN on every exit path, success or failure. The task cancellation handler terminates it as well. The repeated terminate is intentional and is reproduced.
failure_cases: The timeout ends the stream, producing PR-PROVCLI-027's error.
requirements.windows_path: terminate() maps to TerminateProcess and behaves like SIGKILL; acceptable here because the probe persists nothing (port_impacts.md entry 24).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test with a stand-in that never answers, asserting the 20 second bound

requirements.title: Claude's catalog probe fails with a commands message that also destroys the model catalog
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:203-205 - guard let response = message["response"]?["response"], let commands = response["commands"]?.array else { throw ProviderError.failed("Claude could not load its commands.") }
requirements.preconditions: A control_response with request_id handshake arrived.
requirements.expected_result: If response.response is absent, OR response.response.commands is not an array, the probe throws ProviderError.failed with the verbatim message "Claude could not load its commands." (trailing period included). Because models and commands come from this one guard, a missing commands array ALSO destroys the model catalog even though the caller only wanted models. The caller swallows the throw with try?, so no user-visible cause is shown. The coupling is reproduced, not split.

requirements.persistence: The registry leaves attemptedCatalogs unset so it retries later.
failure_cases: This IS the failure path.
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: unit test asserting the exact message and that no models are returned
requirements.upstream_defect: upstream_defects.md entry 6 (handshake commands guard also kills the model catalog, swallowed by try?)

requirements.title: Claude changes permission mode mid-session only when the computed name changed
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:216-221 - runtimeMode = input.runtimeMode; let mode = Self.modeName(...); if mode != permissionMode { _ = try? await control(["subtype": "set_permission_mode", "mode": .string(mode)]); permissionMode = mode }

requirements.title: Claude maps its named tools plus an mcp__ prefix rule to chat rows, returning no row for five
requirements.preconditions: A tool name and its input.
requirements.action: A row is built for a tool call or an approval.
requirements.expected_result: TodoWrite, AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode, EnterPlanMode and ToolSearch return nil, so no row is drawn. Bash -> .command, title input.command or "Shell command", detail input.description. BashOutput, KillShell, KillBash, Monitor, TaskOutput, TaskStop -> .command titled with the tool name itself. Read -> .read, title the relative file_path or "Read file". Write -> .edit, title the relative file_path or "Write file", and with edits enabled one FileEdit(path, old: "", new: input.content). Edit -> .edit, title the relative file_path or "Edit file", one FileEdit from old_string and new_string each defaulting to "". MultiEdit -> .edit with the same fallback and one FileEdit per entry of input.edits. NotebookEdit -> .edit, title the relative notebook_path or "Edit notebook". Glob -> .search, title input.pattern or "Find files", detail the relative path. Grep -> .search, title input.pattern or "Search", detail the relative path. LS -> .search, title the relative path or "List files". WebFetch -> .web, title input.url or "Fetch page". WebSearch -> .web, title input.query or "Search the web". Task and Agent -> .agent, title input.description or "Subagent", detail input.subagent_type. Skill -> .other, title "Skill · " plus input.skill or input.command or the empty string, the separator being U+00B7 with a space each side. Any other name starting with "mcp__" -> .mcp, title "<server> · <tool>" where the name is split on "__" dropping empty parts, server is part 1 or "MCP" and tool is parts 2 onward rejoined with "__" or else the whole name, detail the compact JSON of the input unless it is JSON null. Everything else -> .other titled with the raw tool name.
failure_cases: A missing subject falls back to the literal titles above.
requirements.windows_path: relativePath strips a working-directory prefix that has been given a trailing "/". On Windows, with backslash separators and case-insensitive paths, a literal port fails to make paths relative. requirements.title: Codex maps item types to tool rows, with command actions deciding read, search or command
requirements.preconditions: An item from item/started or item/completed.
requirements.expected_result: "commandExecution": the command is unwrapped of its shell prefix; the set of commandActions types decides the row - a set exactly equal to ["read"] with a first action carrying a path gives .read titled with that path made relative and the command as the detail; a non-empty set that is a SUBSET of ["search", "listFiles"] gives .search titled with the command; otherwise .command titled with the command. "fileChange": .edit titled with the single relative path, or "Edit <n> files" when there is not exactly one. "mcpToolCall": .mcp titled "<server> · <tool>" defaulting to "MCP" and "tool", detail the compact arguments unless that string is "null". "dynamicToolCall": .other titled item.tool or "Tool". "webSearch": .web titled item.query or "Web search". "collabAgentToolCall": .agent whose verb comes from the table spawnAgent -> "Send out a head", sendInput / sendMessage / followupTask -> "Brief a head", wait -> "Wait for heads", closeAgent / interruptAgent -> "Recall a head", resumeAgent -> "Resume a head", listAgents -> "List heads", default -> "Agent"; the title is the prompt flattened to at most 90 characters when present, with the verb as the detail, else the verb as the title with no detail. "subAgentActivity": nil, deliberately, because as rows they only doubled the head's report pill. "imageView": .read titled with the relative item.path or the literal "Image". "imageGeneration": .other titled item.revisedPrompt or "Generate image". "enteredReviewMode" and "exitedReviewMode": .other titled "Review" with item.review as the detail. Anything else: nil.
failure_cases: An unmapped item type draws no row.
requirements.windows_path: unwrapShell strips the literal prefixes "/bin/zsh -lc ", "/bin/bash -lc ", "bash -lc ", "zsh -lc ", "/bin/sh -c " and "sh -c " and the surrounding quotes. On Windows the CLI may wrap commands differently; the prefix list is a PRODUCT constant applied to text the CLI produced and is reproduced as is, since removing an entry changes what the user reads.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over every item type including the three commandExecution shapes

"webSearch", "imageView", "enteredReviewMode" and "exitedReviewMode": status .completed unconditionally, no output. Anything else: status from toolStatus with no exit code.

requirements.windows_path: Diffs arrive from the CLI; line splitting must not be confused by CRLF, since diffStats splits on "\n" and keeps empty subsequences.

requirements.title: Copilot handshake is a ping whose reply need only carry an integer protocolVersion
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CopilotSession.swift:497-502 - let pong = try await connection.request("ping", ["message": "droppy-code"]); guard pong["protocolVersion"]?.int != nil else { connection.close(); throw ProviderError.failed("This `copilot` does not speak the SDK protocol. Update it with `copilot update`.") }
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CopilotSession.swift:22-26 - the header records verification against copilot 1.0.83, protocol version 3
requirements.expected_result: One request with method "ping" and params {"message":"droppy-code"} - the literal value "droppy-code". The reply is accepted when its "protocolVersion" parses as an Int; the VALUE IS NEVER COMPARED, so version 3 is documentation only and any integer passes. On failure the connection is CLOSED and ProviderError.failed is thrown with the verbatim message "This `copilot` does not speak the SDK protocol. Update it with `copilot update`." including both pairs of backticks. There is NO watchdog on this handshake, unlike Codex's 20 second one.
failure_cases: A missing or non-integer protocolVersion: the exact message above.
A CLI that never answers ping hangs indefinitely, because there is no timeout here.
requirements.windows_path: The absence of a watchdog means a Windows CLI that opens but never speaks blocks the calling path. This is upstream behavior and is reproduced; the port must not silently add a timeout.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture on the ping frame plus a unit test on the failure message

requirements.title: Copilot routes a recognized slash command to the CLI instead of prompting with it
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CopilotSession.swift:160-177 - send(_:) with its comment, applyModes, applySelection, beginTurn, then invokeCommand or sendPrompt, with turnActive cleared on a throw
requirements.expected_result: Modes and selection are applied first, then the turn is begun. The text is trimmed and matched against the regular expression ^/([A-Za-z][\w-]*)(?:\s+([\s\S]*))?$ - a leading slash, a name starting with a letter, then word characters or hyphens, optionally followed by whitespace and the rest, which is itself trimmed. requirements.title: Copilot computes a quota percent by two branches that clamp differently, the fallback having no lower bound
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CopilotSession.swift:454-456 - let remaining = snapshot["remainingPercentage"]?.double; let used = snapshot["usedRequests"]?.double ?? 0; let percent = remaining.map { max(0, min(100, 100 - $0)) } ?? min(100, used / entitlement * 100)

requirements.title: Copilot maps its tool names to rows, routing any MCP call by its server name first
requirements.preconditions: A tool name and its arguments.
requirements.expected_result: When an MCP server name is present it wins over every name rule: kind .mcp, title "<server> · <mcpTool or the tool name>", detail the compact arguments unless they are JSON null. Otherwise: the five hidden tools return nil. "bash" and "powershell" -> .command, title arguments.command or "Shell command", detail arguments.description. "read_bash", "write_bash", "stop_bash", "list_bash" -> .command titled humanize(name), detail arguments.shellId. "view" -> .read, title the relative path or "Read file", detail the line range. "create" -> .edit, title the relative path or "Create file", one FileEdit from an empty old and arguments.file_text. "edit" -> .edit, title the relative path or "Edit file", one FileEdit from old_str and new_str. "str_replace_editor" branches on arguments.command: "view" behaves like view; "create" like create; "insert" makes an edit whose old is empty and whose new is new_str; anything else makes an edit from old_str and new_str. "apply_patch" -> .edit, title the single relative patched path or "Edit <n> files", with one path-only FileEdit per file. "grep" -> .search, title arguments.pattern or "Search", detail the relative paths joined by ", " or nil. "glob" -> .search, title arguments.pattern or "Find files", same detail rule. "web_fetch" -> .web, title arguments.url or "Fetch page". "web_search" -> .web, title arguments.query or "Search the web". "task" -> .agent, title arguments.description or "Subagent", detail arguments.name and arguments.agent_type joined by " · " or nil when empty. "read_agent", "write_agent", "list_agents" -> .agent titled humanize(name), detail arguments.agent_id or arguments.message. "skill" -> .other, title "Skill · " plus arguments.skill or the empty string. "sql" -> .other, title arguments.description or "SQL query", detail arguments.query. "create_pull_request" -> .other, title arguments.title or "Create pull request". Anything else -> .other titled humanize(name) with the compact arguments flattened to a single line as the detail, unless they are JSON null. The line range reads a two-element int array and renders "from line <first>" when the second is negative, otherwise "lines <first>–<second>" with an EN DASH (U+2013).

requirements.title: Copilot parses a markdown checklist into todos, treating anything but x and blank as in progress

requirements.title: Command Code's executable name is the bare cmd, with three alternate names and five directories as fallbacks
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:235-249 - the fallback list: which("command-code"), which("commandcode"), which("cmd"), then command-code and cmd under <home>/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, <home>/.npm-global/bin and <home>/.volta/bin
requirements.preconditions: Provider detection is resolving the Command Code CLI.
requirements.expected_result: The primary name is the bare string "cmd". When a custom path is set it is used instead and no fallback is tried. Otherwise PATH is searched for "cmd"; failing that, the fallback list is searched in order and the FIRST executable file wins: which("command-code"), which("commandcode"), which("cmd"), then, for each of <home>/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, <home>/.npm-global/bin and <home>/.volta/bin, the names "command-code" then "cmd". The comment records why: "cmd" is the documented alias and "command-code" and "commandcode" are the package's own names.
requirements.persistence: The resolved path is used for every later spawn.
failure_cases: Nothing resolvable leaves configuration.executable nil, which start() reports as not installed.
requirements.windows_path: THIS IS THE NAMED WINDOWS HAZARD. Resolving the bare name "cmd" through PATH plus PATHEXT on Windows finds C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe, the command interpreter, long before any provider CLI; launching it with this provider's argv would open a console that speaks no protocol on stdout and the session would hang at the first read. The port must therefore validate the EXECUTABLE IDENTITY, not merely the name, before accepting a resolution. The fallback directory list is entirely macOS and Unix package-manager paths and is meaningless on Windows; where an npm or volta install actually puts the Command Code CLI on Windows is not in the pinned source. Both halves are UNK-0006 and neither may be guessed.
requirements.verification_method: a Windows probe recording (a) what PATH plus PATHEXT resolution of "cmd" returns on a clean machine, (b) where the CLI actually installs, and (c) which identity signal distinguishes it - resolved path, file version information, or a handshake the interpreter cannot answer; then a unit test on the chosen rule
requirements.open_question: How the Windows build distinguishes the Command Code provider from the Windows command interpreter, and where the CLI installs on Windows. Neither is in the pinned source. Until this is settled the port must not hard-code any executable name or directory for this provider.

requirements.title: Command Code holds no long-lived process: a session is a conversation and each turn spawns the CLI anew

DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeSession.swift:90-92 - the doc comment plus var isRunning { started && !stopped }

requirements.expected_result: start() spawns NOTHING. isRunning is purely the pair of flags started and !stopped, not any process state - contrast Claude, which asks its process, and Codex and Copilot, which ask their connections. Each send() spawns one `cmd -p` process that lives for exactly one turn and then exits.

requirements.title: Command Code start refuses a resume whose transcript is gone and reports it in one sentence
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeSession.swift:98-102 - guard configuration.executable != nil else throw notInstalled; if let sessionID, !Self.transcriptExists(...) { throw ProviderError.failed("Command Code no longer has this conversation; starting a new one.") }
requirements.preconditions: A resume id that is non-nil and non-empty.
requirements.expected_result: A nil executable throws ProviderError.notInstalled(.commandcode), described as "Command Code is not installed. Install it and sign in with `cmd login`." failure_cases: Blank final text in plan mode produces no plan.
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: unit test in plan and build mode with blank and real text

requirements.title: Command Code's close path clears the turn, withdraws every prompt and deletes the leftover gate files
requirements.expected_result: A close for a process that is no longer the current one returns immediately. Otherwise the stored process is cleared, turnActive becomes false, the current message and reasoning ids are cleared, every pending approval emits .requestResolved and the map is cleared, and EVERY file in the approvals directory is deleted - requests and replies alike - so a stale one never answers a later call. Then, when the session was stopped, the method returns without any turn event.
failure_cases: A failed delete is ignored.
requirements.cancellation: A stop suppresses the turn outcome entirely.
requirements.windows_path: Deleting files the CLI may still hold open can fail on Windows; the failures are ignored, but a stale request file that survives could be picked up by the next turn's scan. The port should verify that the reply files are keyed by tool call id so a survivor cannot answer a different call (PA-0015).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test asserting the directory is empty after a turn and that a locked file does not throw

requirements.title: Command Code reports an interrupted turn on the interrupt flag or exit code 130, before anything else
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeSession.swift:445-448 - if interruptRequested || status == 130 { onEvent?(.turnCompleted(status: .interrupted, error: nil)); return }
requirements.expected_result: This test comes FIRST, before the result line is consulted. When interruptRequested is true OR the exit status is exactly 130, the turn is reported .interrupted with a nil error and nothing further is evaluated - even if a result line arrived.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: Exit code 130 is the POSIX convention for a SIGINT-terminated process and does not arise on Windows. TerminateProcess reports whatever code it was given, so the 130 test must be RELAXED for Windows while the interruptRequested test carries the behavior. The port must choose and record the Windows termination exit code deliberately (port_impacts.md entry 24).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test asserting an interrupted turn on Windows reports .interrupted through the flag alone

requirements.title: Command Code closes a turn from its result line, treating a turn cap as a completion with a warning
requirements.preconditions: A result line arrived and the turn was not interrupted.
requirements.expected_result: subtype "success": the turn is .completed, and when stopReason is exactly "max_turns" the turn-cap notice fires first. subtype "max_turns": the notice fires and the turn is ALSO reported .completed, not failed. Any other subtype: the error text is the result's error, else the stored run error, else the last lines of the process's stderr tail, else the literal "Command Code stopped before finishing."; when isRateLimit matches that text a .usageLimit(resetsAt: nil) is emitted FIRST; then .turnCompleted(.failed, friendlyError(text)). The turn-cap notice is a WARNING reading "Command Code stopped at its cap of 400 round trips for one message. Send another to carry on." with the number interpolated from the maxTurns constant, and it is SUPPRESSED entirely when the turn was a final report.
failure_cases: Every failure path above.
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test over each subtype and a final-report turn hitting the cap

requirements.title: Command Code maps nine exit codes to exact outcomes when no result line arrived
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeSession.swift:464-489 - the exit-code switch with its comment
requirements.preconditions: The process exited with NO result line and the turn was not interrupted.
requirements.expected_result: The stderr tail is TextCleanup.lastLines of the process's error tail. Then, verbatim: 0 -> .completed with no error. 3 -> .failed, "Command Code is not signed in. Run `cmd login` in Terminal, or add a Studio API key in Settings → Providers → Command Code." 4 -> .failed, the tail or "Command Code was denied permission." 5 -> a .usageLimit(resetsAt: nil) FIRST, then .failed with the tail or "Command Code is rate limited. Wait for the window to reset, or buy on-demand credits, which are never throttled." 6 -> .failed, "Could not reach Command Code. Check the connection and try again." 7 -> .failed, the tail or "Command Code's API returned a server error. Try again in a moment." 8 -> the turn-cap notice, then .completed. 9 -> .failed, "The model produced no response." 10 -> .failed, "Command Code is out of credits. Top up at commandcode.ai/billing, or wait for the monthly credits to reset." Any other code -> .failed with the stored run error, else the tail, else "Command Code exited with code <status>." Note the arrows in the code-3 message are U+2192 RIGHTWARDS ARROW.
failure_cases: Every branch above is a failure path except 0 and 8.
requirements.windows_path: These are the CLI's own exit codes and are platform-neutral, but a Windows process terminated by the app reports a DIFFERENT code that must not collide with 3 to 10; the termination code must be chosen so it falls through to the default branch or is caught by the interrupt flag first.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test driving a stand-in to exit with each code, asserting the exact message

requirements.title: Command Code detects a rate limit from three lowercased substrings
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeSession.swift:497-500 - isRateLimit matches "rate limit", "usage exceeded" or "window limit"
requirements.expected_result: The text is lowercased and matched against exactly three substrings: "rate limit", "usage exceeded", "window limit". Any match emits a .usageLimit(resetsAt: nil) before the failure. There is no reset time, so the app cannot say when the window reopens.
failure_cases: No match: no usage-limit event.
requirements.windows_path: The lowercasing must be invariant.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over all three substrings and a near miss

requirements.title: Command Code rewrites two families of account errors into actionable sentences
requirements.expected_result: The text is lowercased for the tests. When it contains "not authenticated" OR "unauthorized" OR "session expired", the whole message is REPLACED by "Command Code is not signed in. Run `cmd login` in Terminal, or add a Studio API key in Settings → Providers → Command Code." When it contains "insufficient credits" OR "out of credits", it is replaced by "Command Code is out of credits. Top up at commandcode.ai/billing, or wait for the monthly credits to reset." Both replacements are identical to the exit-code 3 and 10 messages. Otherwise the original text is returned unchanged. The sign-in test is evaluated first, so a message containing both families reports sign-in.
failure_cases: No match: the CLI's own wording survives.
requirements.windows_path: The lowercasing must be invariant. On Windows the sentence still names `cmd login` in Terminal; whether that instruction is accurate for the Windows CLI is part of UNK-0006 and must not be reworded without evidence.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over both families and a plain error

requirements.title: Command Code extracts error text from a string, a message field or the compact JSON
requirements.preconditions: An error value from a result, a run_error or a tool_errored frame.
requirements.expected_result: A nil or JSON-null value yields nil. A bare string yields that string, or nil when it is empty. Otherwise a non-empty "message" field yields that. Otherwise the compact JSON serialization yields that, except that the literal "{}" yields nil.
failure_cases: An empty object yields nil, so the caller falls back to its own default.
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over all four shapes

requirements.title: Command Code reads content-block text, rendering an image block as a bracketed marker
requirements.preconditions: A content value from a message or tool result.
requirements.expected_result: A nil or JSON-null value yields the empty string. A bare string yields itself. An array yields, per block, the block's "text" when it is a string, else the literal "[image]" when the block's type is exactly "image", else nothing; the contributions are joined by a single newline. Anything else yields the empty string.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over a string, a mixed array and a null

requirements.title: Command Code todo parsing accepts three text keys and five status strings
requirements.expected_result: Each entry of input.todos needs a string under "content", else "text", else "title"; entries with none are skipped. Status "completed" OR "done" -> .done; "in_progress" OR "active" -> .active; anything else, including a missing status, -> .pending. This is broader than Claude's parser, which reads only "content" and only two status strings.
failure_cases: A missing todos array yields an empty list, which is still emitted.
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over all three text keys and all five status strings

requirements.title: Command Code maps its tool names to rows, with an mcp__ rule and a length-capped fallback detail
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeSession.swift:622-627 - humanize splits on underscores and capitalizes only the first word
requirements.preconditions: A tool name and its input.
requirements.action: A row is built for a call or an approval.
requirements.expected_result: "shell_command" and "powershell" -> .command, title the unwrapped input.command or "Shell command", detail input.description, and when run_in_background is true the detail gains " · in the background" appended after any existing detail. "monitor_command" -> .command, title the unwrapped command or "Monitor command". "shell_output" -> .command titled "Shell output", detail input.id or input.task_id. "shell_tasks" -> .command titled "Shell tasks". "kill_shell" -> .command titled "Stop shell", detail input.id or input.task_id or the decimal input.pid. "read_file" -> .read, title the relative file_path or path or "Read file", and when BOTH offset and limit are ints the detail is "lines <offset>–<offset + limit>" with an EN DASH. "read_directory" -> .search, title the relative path or "List files". "write_file" -> .edit, title the relative file_path or "Write file", with one FileEdit from the snapshot (or the empty string) to input.content. "edit_file" -> .edit, title the relative file_path or path or "Edit file", with one FileEdit whose old is old_string or old_text or old or the empty string and whose new is new_string or new_text or new or the empty string. "glob" -> .search, title input.pattern or "Find files", detail the relative path. "grep" -> .search, title input.pattern or "Search", detail the relative path and input.glob joined by " · " or nil when empty. "web_fetch" -> .web, title input.url or "Fetch page". "web_search" -> .web, title input.query or "Search the web". "agent" -> .agent, title input.description, else input.prompt flattened to 96 characters, else "Sub-agent"; detail input.subagent_type. "agent_output" -> .agent titled "Agent output", detail input.agent_id. "activate_skill" -> .other, title "Skill · " plus input.name or the empty string. "enter_worktree" and "exit_worktree" -> .other titled humanize(name), detail input.name. "run_command" -> .other, title "Command · " plus input.command or input.name or the empty string. Any other name starting with "mcp__" -> .mcp titled "<server> · <tool>" by the same split rule Claude uses, detail the compact input unless JSON null. Everything else -> .other titled humanize(name), with the compact input as the detail ONLY when it is non-empty, is not "{}" and is at most 300 characters. humanize splits on underscores and capitalizes ONLY the first word, so "task_create" becomes "Task create".
failure_cases: Missing subjects fall back to the literals above.
requirements.windows_path: relativePath has the same prefix-stripping caveat as PR-PROVCLI-062. Note that "powershell" is a first-class tool name here, so a Windows CLI that prefers it produces the same row shape as bash.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over every named tool, an mcp__ name, an unknown name and a 400-character input

requirements.title: Command Code watches the approvals directory for writes and rescans on every event
requirements.expected_result: Any previous watcher is cancelled first. The directory is opened for event notification only; a failure to open leaves NO watcher, and the gate then works only through the scan that tool_queued triggers. A filesystem object source is created for the WRITE event mask, delivering on the main queue, whose handler calls scanApprovals. Its cancel handler closes the descriptor. stopWatcher cancels and clears it.
side_effects: An open file descriptor and a dispatch source for the life of the session
failure_cases: A failed open silently degrades to scan-on-tool-queued only.
requirements.windows_path: There is no equivalent of a write-masked file-descriptor event source; the Windows implementation must use directory change notification for the same directory and deliver on the UI thread, and it must still tolerate missing events, because the source already falls back to an explicit scan at tool_queued. The mapping is a named platform boundary.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test writing a request file and asserting the prompt appears without a tool_queued frame

requirements.title: Command Code scans request files in lexicographic order and deletes each as it reads it
requirements.preconditions: A turn is active and an approvals directory exists.
requirements.action: scanApprovals runs, from the watcher or from tool_queued.
requirements.expected_result: The scan returns immediately when there is no directory or no active turn. The directory is listed; a failure returns. Files are sorted by their LAST PATH COMPONENT, ascending, and only those whose name ends with the literal suffix ".request.json" are considered. Each is read and parsed; an unreadable or unparseable file is SKIPPED and left in place. A parsed file is DELETED IMMEDIATELY after reading. The id is request.toolCallId when a string, else the file name with ".request.json" removed. A request whose id already has a pending approval is skipped. Otherwise it is decided.
failure_cases: An unparseable request file is left behind and rescanned on every event, forever, until the turn ends and clearApprovalFiles removes it.
requirements.cancellation: A finished turn clears the directory.
requirements.windows_path: The sort must be ordinal on the file name, not culture-sensitive. Deleting a file the mod may still have open can fail on Windows; a failed delete leaves the request in place, and the pending-approval check is what stops it being asked twice (PA-0015).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test with two request files asserting the order, plus one unparseable file

requirements.title: Command Code auto-approves by runtime mode, with a four-name allow list and a write-classification test in Auto
requirements.preconditions: A request read from the gate.
requirements.expected_result: The approval row is built first. The request is auto-allowed when autoApproves is true OR the session already holds a grant for that row's kind. autoApproves: isEdit is (name == "write_file" || name == "edit_file"). .fullAccess -> true, although the comment records it never reaches here because Full access loads no gate. .supervised -> false, always. .autoAcceptEdits -> isEdit. .auto -> true for an edit; otherwise, for the exactly three shell names "shell_command", "powershell" and "monitor_command", the negation of ShellCommandKind.mayWriteFiles(input.command ?? ""); otherwise true for the exactly four names "kill_shell", "cron_create", "cron_delete" and "task_stop"; otherwise false. An auto-allowed request is replied to at once; anything else is stored as pending and emitted as an .approval.
side_effects: A reply file written, or a provider event
failure_cases: An unclassifiable command counts as writing and is asked, which is the safe answer.
requirements.windows_path: ShellCommandKind.mayWriteFiles classifies the command TEXT THE MODEL PRODUCED, so its reader lists are a product constant, not a platform constant, and must be ported verbatim (PA-0011). Whether the Windows build additionally needs Windows tool names depends on what shell the CLI runs commands in on Windows, which is UNK-0005 and must not be guessed.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over all four runtime modes crossed with an edit, a read-only shell command, a writing shell command and each allow-list name

requirements.title: Command Code approvals always offer the same three options and carry a tool item id only for a known call
requirements.expected_result: The row is built by makeToolCall with the recorded snapshot. The approval kind is .command for a command row, .fileChange for an edit row and .tool for everything else. The options are ALWAYS exactly three, in this order: "allow"/"Approve"/.approve, "always"/"Approve for session"/.approveAlways, "deny"/"Decline"/.decline - unlike Claude and Copilot, the session option is never hidden. The toolItemID is the request id ONLY when a tool with that id was already recorded from tool_queued, and nil otherwise, so a prompt that arrives before its row does not point at a missing row. grantKey maps .command to "command", .fileChange to "fileChange" and .tool, .permissions and .plan all to "tool".
requirements.persistence: Session grants live for the life of the session object only.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over each row kind and a request with no matching tool row

requirements.title: Command Code resolves an approval by writing a reply file and records a session grant for always
requirements.preconditions: A pending approval keyed by requestID.
requirements.expected_result: An unknown id does nothing. For "allow" or "always" the request is allowed; "always" ALSO inserts the row's grant key into the session grants, so every later request of that kind is auto-allowed for the rest of the session. Anything else denies. .requestResolved is emitted. The reply payload is verbatim: {"decision":"allow"} to allow, and {"decision":"deny","reason":"The user declined this in Droppy Code. Do not retry it; take another approach or explain what you would need."} to deny. It is written to "<id>.reply.json" by writing "<id>.reply.json.tmp" atomically and then replacing the target; if that fails, it falls back to writing the target directly and atomically, with any failure ignored.
side_effects: One or two files written; one provider event
requirements.persistence: The reply file is consumed and deleted by the mod.
failure_cases: A failed write leaves the mod polling until the turn ends or its six-hour deadline passes.
requirements.windows_path: The temp-then-replace sequence must be an atomic replace on Windows, because the mod polls the target file and must never read a partial write. A replace can fail while the mod has the file open; the direct-write fallback is what covers that, and it must also be atomic.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture asserting both payloads byte for byte, plus a test where the replace fails

requirements.title: The Command Code approval mod is a TypeScript file rewritten only when its bytes change
requirements.expected_result: The support directory is created with intermediate directories. The file is named exactly "droppy-code-approvals.ts". The mod text is encoded as UTF-8 and compared BYTE FOR BYTE against whatever is on disk; it is written atomically ONLY when they differ, so a new build's mod replaces the old one and an unchanged one is left alone. The file URL is returned. A write failure propagates.
side_effects: A directory created; possibly one file written
requirements.persistence: The mod file persists between runs under the app's support directory.
failure_cases: A failed write throws out of start().
requirements.windows_path: Keep the byte-compare-before-write and the atomic write, because the CLI may be reading the file concurrently (port_impacts.md entry 22). The support tree moves to the Windows data directory.
requirements.verification_method: restart test asserting the file is not rewritten when unchanged

requirements.title: The Command Code mod lets twenty-six read-only tools through without ever waiting on the user
requirements.preconditions: The mod is loaded with an approvals directory set.
requirements.action: A tool is about to run.
requirements.expected_result: The beforeToolCall hook returns immediately, allowing the call, when the tool name is in this exact set, in source order: read_file, read_directory, glob, grep, shell_output, shell_tasks, todo_write, task_create, task_update, task_list, task_get, sleep, web_search, web_fetch, agent, agent_output, activate_skill, taste, get_diagnostics, ask_user_question, plan_review, enter_plan_mode, exit_plan_mode, cron_list, run_command. Note that run_command IS in this read-only set even though it is not a read-only operation by name; that is the shipped list and it is reproduced as is.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: None; this list lives inside the shipped TypeScript and is copied verbatim.
requirements.verification_method: a byte-for-byte comparison of the shipped mod text against the source

requirements.title: The Command Code mod registers MCP tools from the bridge and swallows every bridge error
requirements.preconditions: DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE is set in the environment.
requirements.expected_result: When the bridge path is set, the module is imported asynchronously and, for each tool it lists, cmd.addTool is called with schema name "mcp__" + server + "__" + name, the tool's description, and its inputSchema as input_schema; the run function calls the tool with the input or an empty object and returns {ok: true, content: [{type: 'text', text}]}. Any error from the import or the registration is caught and logged with console.error('droppy mcp', error) and otherwise SWALLOWED, so MCP failure never blocks the gate. The registration is not awaited, so a slow bridge can leave tools unregistered for the first part of a run.
side_effects: Tools registered in the CLI; stderr output on failure
failure_cases: A failing bridge leaves the MCP tools simply absent.
requirements.windows_path: The bridge path is handed to a dynamic import inside the CLI; a Windows path may need a file URL for that import to succeed. This must be probed against the real CLI, not assumed.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test with a stand-in bridge, and a probe of the import form the CLI accepts on Windows

requirements.title: The Command Code mod sanitizes the call id, writes a request file atomically and polls for a reply every 40 ms
requirements.preconditions: A non-read-only tool call with DROPPY_CODE_APPROVALS set.
requirements.expected_result: With no approvals directory the hook registers NOTHING at all and every tool passes. Otherwise: the id is the toolCallId, or, when absent, `${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`, with every character outside A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore, period and hyphen replaced by an underscore. Any stale reply file is unlinked. The request is written to "<id>.request.json.tmp" and RENAMED onto "<id>.request.json", carrying {toolCallId: <the sanitized id>, toolName, input}. Then the hook polls: it reads the reply file; when present it unlinks it, parses it (a parse failure yields an empty object), and returns nothing when answer.decision is exactly 'allow', otherwise {block: true, additionalContext: answer.reason || 'The user declined this in Droppy Code.'}. Between polls it sleeps 40 milliseconds.
side_effects: Files written, renamed and deleted; a busy-ish poll loop for the life of the prompt
requirements.persistence: The request file is the channel; the app deletes it as it reads it.
failure_cases: A reply that is not valid JSON blocks the call with the default decline text.
requirements.windows_path: The rename onto an existing name must be an atomic replace on Windows. The sanitized id becomes a FILE NAME, and the allowed character set already excludes every Windows-illegal character, so no additional sanitization is needed or permitted.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture driving the real mod text under a stand-in runtime, asserting the file names and payloads

requirements.title: The Command Code mod gives up on an abort signal, an orphaned parent or a six-hour deadline
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeAPI.swift:424-431 - the abort, ppid and deadline checks
requirements.preconditions: The hook is polling for a reply.
requirements.action: One of the three exit conditions is met.
requirements.expected_result: When ctx.signal.aborted becomes true, the request file is unlinked and the hook returns {block: true, additionalContext: 'The turn was stopped.'} When process.ppid is exactly 1, OR more than 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000 milliseconds have passed since the request was written, the request file is unlinked and the hook returns {block: true, additionalContext: 'Droppy Code did not answer.'} All three messages are verbatim.
failure_cases: These ARE the failure paths.
requirements.cancellation: The abort signal is the CLI's own cancellation reaching the mod.
requirements.windows_path: process.ppid === 1 is the POSIX orphan test and is MEANINGLESS on Windows, where an orphaned process keeps its original parent id or reports a reused one. That check therefore never fires on Windows and the six-hour deadline becomes the only backstop. This is an observable behavioural difference that must be recorded rather than silently replaced, because changing the shipped mod text changes the gate for every run.
requirements.verification_method: a probe recording what process.ppid reports on Windows after the app exits, then a decision recorded as an engineering decision with that evidence
requirements.open_question: Whether the Windows build ships the mod text unchanged, accepting that the orphan check never fires and a stranded gate waits six hours, or adds a Windows-valid orphan test. Changing the shipped TypeScript is a product change to a security-relevant gate and is not made without a decision.

requirements.title: Command Code resolves the API key from the environment first, then the stored login
requirements.preconditions: A read of the account's plan, credits or auth state.
requirements.expected_result: COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY from the environment, trimmed of whitespace and newlines, wins whenever it is non-empty - which is how a key pasted into Settings reaches both the CLI and these reads. Otherwise the stored login is read from <home>/.commandcode/auth.json, where home is environment["HOME"] when non-empty else LoginEnvironment.homeDirectory; the file must parse and carry a non-empty trimmed "apiKey", and the user name is "userName" or "name". A missing or unparseable file yields nil.
failure_cases: No key anywhere: the plan, credits and auth reads all return their own nil or signed-out results.
requirements.windows_path: HOME is normally unset on Windows, so the home fallback carries this. The path segment uses a forward slash and must be joined as components.
requirements.verification_method: unit test with the environment key set, with only the file, and with neither

requirements.title: Command Code auth status asks the CLI only when a key exists, and reads three signals out of its output
requirements.action: Settings reads the Command Code sign-in state.
requirements.expected_result: With no API key at all the CLI is NOT asked and .signedOut is returned at once. Otherwise Shell.run(executable, ["status", "--no-auto-update"], environment:, timeout: 25) runs; a throw returns .unknown. ANSI is stripped from stdout plus stderr. Then, in order: a regular-expression match of "Authenticated as " followed by one or more non-space characters returns .signedIn with that captured name; an exit status of exactly 3, or text containing "not authenticated" or "not logged in" case-insensitively, returns .signedOut; text containing "authentication verified" case-insensitively returns .signedIn with the stored login's user name, which may be nil; anything else returns .unknown.
side_effects: One short-lived child process, bounded at 25 seconds
failure_cases: An unreachable CLI: .unknown, never .signedOut.
requirements.windows_path: ANSI stripping is load-bearing on Windows. The argv is ["status", "--no-auto-update"] on the SAME executable that PR-PROVCLI-203 must validate; running it against the Windows command interpreter would open a console rather than answer.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over each of the four output shapes

requirements.title: Command Code reads two dollar-capped windows and a plan name from two billing routes fetched concurrently
requirements.action: The usage panel reads Command Code's limits.
requirements.expected_result: With no key, nil. Otherwise "/alpha/billing/credits" and "/alpha/billing/subscriptions" are fetched CONCURRENTLY. A nil credits response returns nil regardless of the subscription. The window limits object is credits.windowLimits or JSON null. Exactly two entries are walked in this fixed order: key "fiveHour" with the title stem "5-hour limit", then key "weekly" with the stem "Weekly". Each needs a present, non-null window whose "cap" is a double greater than zero; otherwise it is skipped. used is window.used or zero. The window id is the KEY. The title is "<stem> · <ProviderCredits.money(cap, currency: "USD")>" - space, U+00B7, space. The percent is min(100, (used / cap) * 100), clamped only at the top. resetAt is window.resetAt read as epoch MILLISECONDS, treated as absent when it is not greater than zero. The plan name comes from subscription.data.planId. The result is nil when there are no windows AND no plan name; otherwise a PlanLimits with that plan name and those windows. Each fetch is a 15 second request carrying Authorization "Bearer <key>" and Accept "application/json", and anything but HTTP 200 yields nil.
requirements.persistence: The registry persists the plan limits.
failure_cases: A non-200 or unparseable response yields nil for that route.
requirements.windows_path: Network only; the same TLS trust and proxy configuration as the rest of the app applies.
requirements.verification_method: unit test against recorded responses, including a zero cap and a zero resetAt

requirements.title: Command Code credits sum three dollar balances and report usability from a threshold flag
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeAPI.swift:103-125 - credits(environment:) and credits(apiKey:) with the doc comment
requirements.expected_result: With no key, nil. "/alpha/billing/credits" is fetched; a nil response, or a missing or JSON-null "credits" object, yields nil. monthly = credits.monthlyCredits or zero; purchased = credits.purchasedCredits or zero; free = credits.freeCredits or zero. The result carries total = monthly + purchased + free, currency the literal "USD", toppedUp = purchased, granted = free, monthly = monthly, and isUsable = (credits.belowThreshold != true) - so a MISSING flag counts as usable and only an explicit true marks the account as unable to be charged. The billing page linked from the UI is https://commandcode.ai/billing.
failure_cases: Any failure yields nil and the balance shows as unknown.
requirements.windows_path: Network only.
requirements.verification_method: unit test against a recorded response with and without belowThreshold

requirements.title: Command Code maps eight known plan ids and reads an unfamiliar one out of its own words
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeAPI.swift:127-166 - the planNames table and planName(_:) with both doc comments
requirements.preconditions: A plan id from the billing API.
requirements.expected_result: A nil or empty id yields nil. The lowercased id is looked up in this exact table: "individual-go" -> "Go"; "individual-goat" -> "GOAT"; "individual-pro" -> "Pro"; "individual-pro-v1" -> "Pro"; "individual-provider" -> "Provider"; "individual-max" -> "Max 10×"; "individual-ultra" -> "Max 20×"; "teams-pro" -> "Teams Pro". The two multipliers use U+00D7. On a miss the id is split on hyphens, a leading "individual" part is dropped, and an empty remainder yields nil; otherwise each part is mapped: "goat" -> "GOAT", "pro" -> "Pro", "go" -> "Go", "max" -> "Max", "ultra" -> "Ultra", "teams" or "team" -> "Teams", a part matching one or more digits followed by a lowercase x -> those digits plus "×", and anything else -> its first character uppercased followed by the rest unchanged. The parts are joined by single spaces, so an unfamiliar plan never shows as nothing.
requirements.persistence: Part of the persisted plan limits.
failure_cases: An id that is only "individual" yields nil.
requirements.windows_path: The lowercasing and uppercasing must be invariant. The U+00D7 characters must survive to the UI.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over all eight table ids, an individual-max-20x style id and a bare unknown

requirements.title: Command Code lists models from the CLI's own printed table, keeping one default
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeAPI.swift:179-234 - listModels and parseModels with the doc comment
requirements.action: The registry loads the Command Code catalog.
requirements.expected_result: Shell.run(executable, ["--list-models", "--no-auto-update"], environment:, timeout: 30) runs and its STDOUT is ANSI-stripped. The user's config.json supplies the configured model from "model" and the configured efforts object from "reasoningEffort". Parsing: each line is trimmed; empty lines are skipped; lines beginning with "Available models", "Pass the full id", "cmd ", "Docs:" or "Usage" are skipped. A line matching one or more non-space characters, then TWO OR MORE spaces, then the rest, is a model row; the id must contain a hyphen or a slash or the row is skipped. The detail is the remainder trimmed, with the literal " (recommended)" and " (default)" substrings REMOVED and each setting its own flag. The option carries id, name = displayName(for: id), detail = the section header and the remaining detail joined by " · " with nils dropped, efforts = efforts(for: id), defaultEffort = the configured efforts object indexed by the id, and isDefault = recommended or CLI-default, further forced true when the id matches the configured model. A non-matching line becomes the current SECTION HEADER when it has no space and starts with an uppercase letter, or when it is shorter than 24 characters. Finally: when a configured model matches a row, every other row's isDefault is cleared and that row is MOVED to index 0; otherwise the first row already marked default becomes the only default and nothing is reordered. An empty result throws ProviderError.failed with the last lines of stderr plus stdout, or the literal "Command Code listed no models."
side_effects: One short-lived child process, bounded at 30 seconds; a config file read
failure_cases: The exact fallback message above.
requirements.windows_path: ANSI stripping is load-bearing. The two-or-more-space column split is applied to text the CLI printed; a Windows console that pads differently would change which rows parse, so the real output must be captured on Windows before this is called verified.
requirements.verification_method: unit test against a captured --list-models output, plus a Windows capture comparison

requirements.title: Command Code matches a model id case-insensitively by full id or by the name after the slash
requirements.expected_result: Both sides are lowercased. An exact equality returns true at once. Otherwise each side is reduced to the part after its LAST slash (or the whole string when there is none) and those are compared for equality. So "moonshotai/kimi-k3" matches "kimi-k3" and vice versa. This same function backs the context-window fallback lookup.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: The lowercasing must be invariant.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over an exact match, a short-name match and a non-match

requirements.title: Command Code builds a model display name by merging version digits and special-casing five token forms
requirements.expected_result: The id is reduced to the part after its last slash, then to the part before the first colon; a ":free" anywhere in the short id contributes the suffix " Free". The remainder is split on hyphens. Then, scanning left to right, any two ADJACENT all-digit tokens are merged with a period between them and the second removed, repeatedly, so "claude-fable-5-1" reads as Fable 5.1. Each token is then mapped: "gpt" -> "GPT"; "glm" -> "GLM"; "hy3" and "hy4" -> uppercased; "v4", "v4.1" and "v2.5" -> uppercased; a token starting with a digit -> unchanged; anything else -> its first character uppercased plus the rest. Finally, when the first word is exactly "GPT" and there is more than one word, the result is "GPT-" plus the remaining words joined by single spaces plus the suffix; otherwise all words joined by single spaces plus the suffix.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: The case changes must be invariant.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over claude-sonnet-5, moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code, gpt-5.6-terra, claude-fable-5-1 and a :free id

requirements.title: Pi runs strict LF-delimited JSONL and reports a launch failure with a wrapped message
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiSession.swift:112-133 - StdioProcess with framing: .lines; do/catch throwing ProviderError.failed("Pi could not start: \(error.localizedDescription)"); the read task then awaits the exit and calls didClose(status:)

A start failure throws ProviderError.failed with "Pi could not start: " followed by the underlying error's localized description; note the process reference is assigned AFTER the successful start, so a failed launch leaves none. A read Task consumes each message through handle(_:), then awaits the exit status and calls didClose with it.

requirements.title: Pi's handshake is get_state then get_commands, with no initialize and no version negotiation
requirements.preconditions: The process started and the reader attached.
requirements.expected_result: There is NO initialize. First a request {"type":"get_state"} is sent. Its payload is read from the reply's "data" when present, else from the reply itself. A non-empty "sessionFile" string becomes the session id; failing that, a non-empty "sessionId" string does. The context window is taken from data.model.contextWindow. .sessionReady is emitted with the session id or the EMPTY STRING. Then a request {"type":"get_commands"} is sent, its payload read the same way, and each entry of "commands" with a string "name" becomes a SlashCommand with that name and its "description" or the empty string; a non-empty list is emitted as .commands. Finally started becomes true and stopped false, and start() returns the session id or the empty string.
side_effects: Two stdin lines; up to two provider events
requirements.persistence: The session id is the thread's persisted resume id.
failure_cases: Neither request can fail: both resolve with JSON null after 30 seconds (PR-PROVCLI-276).
requirements.windows_path: None beyond the framing.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture comparing both request lines and a unit test over both reply shapes

requirements.title: Pi requests are numbered droppy-<n> from 1 and resolve with JSON null after thirty seconds instead of throwing
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiSession.swift:302-309 - the response case resolving pendingResponses by id
requirements.expected_result: With no process the call returns JSON null at once. Otherwise requestCounter is incremented BEFORE use, so the first id is exactly "droppy-1"; the literal prefix is "droppy-", NOT "droppy-code-" as Claude uses. The id is added to the request object and the line written. The continuation resolves when a line arrives whose type is "response" and whose id matches. A detached Task sleeps exactly 30 seconds and, if the continuation is still pending, resolves it with JSON NULL. The timeout NEVER THROWS. The consequence, recorded as an upstream oddity: a hung get_state leaves start() returning an EMPTY session id rather than reporting an error, and the thread then believes it has a session it cannot resume.
failure_cases: A hung CLI silently produces an empty session id and an empty command list.
requirements.cancellation: The 30 second timer is the only bound.
requirements.windows_path: None. The id prefix is a contract with the app's own reader and is not renamed with the product.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test with a stand-in that never answers get_state, asserting start() returns an empty id after 30 seconds
requirements.upstream_defect: provider-argv-and-handshakes.md section 10 item 8 (Pi's 30 second timeout resolves null silently, so start() can return an empty session id)

requirements.title: Pi rewrites the gate file before every turn, so mode changes take effect per turn while the launch flag does not

It is rewritten before EVERY turn, so finalReport and both modes are per-turn, while the --approve / --no-approve flag is fixed at launch. A runtime mode change mid-session therefore changes the gate's behaviour but NOT the CLI flag. The raw values are camelCase: supervised, autoAcceptEdits, auto, fullAccess, and build, plan.

The object must be hand-written rather than produced by a generic enum serializer, and the write must keep write-temp-then-replace semantics because the extension polls while the app rewrites (port_impacts.md entry 21).

requirements.title: Pi refuses a second turn while one is running and re-reads the context window after a model switch
