requirements.title: Pi handles thirteen inbound line types, including a failed prompt response that ends the turn
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiSession.swift:300-344 - handle(_:) over response, message_start, message_update, message_end, tool_execution_start, tool_execution_update, tool_execution_end, agent_end, compaction_start, compaction_end, auto_retry_start, extension_error, extension_ui_request, with a default that breaks
requirements.expected_result: Exactly these thirteen types are handled; anything else is ignored. A "response" with a matching pending id resolves it; a response with NO matching pending id but whose "command" is exactly "prompt" and whose "success" is exactly false sets the turn error to its "error", else its "message", else the literal "Pi reported an error.", and FINISHES THE TURN. message_start requires message.role to be exactly "assistant"; it increments the message counter, sets the current message id, and clears both the accumulated message text and reasoning text and the current reasoning id. tool_execution_update emits .toolOutput with the text of partialResult.content when non-empty. agent_end finishes the turn. compaction_start emits an INFO notice reading "Compacting the conversation…" with a horizontal-ellipsis character (U+2026) and no period; compaction_end emits an INFO notice reading "Conversation compacted" with NO trailing period. auto_retry_start emits a WARNING notice with the line's "error" or the literal "Pi is retrying." extension_error emits an ERROR notice with the line's "error" or the literal "Pi reported an extension error."
failure_cases: A failed prompt response ends the turn as failed.
requirements.windows_path: The ellipsis and the missing trailing periods are verbatim user-visible text and must survive as UTF-8.
requirements.verification_method: unit test feeding one line of every type plus an unknown one

Note these have NO "cc-" prefix and use a hyphen before the counter, unlike Command Code's "cc-<launchID>-m<n>"; the two shapes must not be unified.

requirements.title: Pi accumulates text and thinking deltas and reports usage from a total or four named fallback pairs
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiSession.swift:346-381 - handleUpdate, including the comment at :371-374 explaining why each part is named
requirements.expected_result: The event is message.assistantMessageEvent, else message.event, else JSON null. A "text_delta" with a non-empty delta mints a message id if none is open, accumulates and emits .messageDelta. A "thinking_delta" with a non-empty delta mints a reasoning id if none is open AND clears the accumulated reasoning text at that moment, accumulates and emits .reasoningDelta. Then, on EVERY update regardless of the event type, usage is read from message.usage, else event.usage, else JSON null: used is usage.totalTokens when present, otherwise the sum of (usage.input or usage.inputTokens or 0) + (usage.output or usage.outputTokens or 0) + (usage.cacheRead or usage.cacheReadTokens or 0) + (usage.cacheWrite or usage.cacheWriteTokens or 0). When used is greater than zero, .usage is emitted with that count and the stored context window. The four parts are named separately because the single-expression form made the Swift type checker give up; the arithmetic is unchanged and must be reproduced exactly.
failure_cases: Zero usage emits nothing.
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over a total-bearing payload and one using all four fallback pairs

requirements.title: Pi completes a message from its content blocks when they are non-empty, and records the reply for plan mode
requirements.expected_result: A message whose role is not exactly "assistant" is ignored. The final text starts as the accumulated delta text; when message.content is an array, the "text" fields of its blocks whose type is exactly "text" are joined with NO separator, and that joined string REPLACES the final text when it is non-empty. When a reasoning id is open and its accumulated text is not blank, .reasoningCompleted is emitted; the reasoning id is then cleared either way. When a message id is open, .messageCompleted is emitted with the final text and that text is recorded as lastReplyText, which plan mode later hands over as the plan; the message id is then cleared. Finally, when message.stopReason is exactly "error", the turn error becomes message.errorMessage or the literal "Pi reported an error."
failure_cases: A non-assistant message is ignored entirely.
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over a streamed message, a whole message and an error stop reason

requirements.title: Pi maps six tool-name groups to row kinds and snapshots a file before a write
requirements.preconditions: A tool_execution_start line with a call id and a tool name.
requirements.expected_result: The arguments are message.args, else message.input, else JSON null; the name and arguments are recorded. A tool named exactly "write" with a string "path" takes a snapshot of that file first, storing the empty string when the snapshot is nil. The kind is: "bash" -> .command; "read" -> .read; "edit" and "write" -> .edit; "grep", "find" and "ls" -> .search; any name starting with "mcp__" -> .mcp; everything else -> .other. The title and detail are: bash -> the unwrapped args.command or the literal "bash", no detail; read, edit and write -> the relative args.path or the tool name, no detail; grep and find -> args.pattern or the tool name, no detail; ls -> args.path or the literal ".", no detail; an mcp__ name -> "<server> · <tool>" by the same split rule Claude uses, with the PRETTY-printed arguments as the detail unless they are null or compact to "{}"; anything else -> the raw tool name with the same pretty-printed detail rule. One .toolStarted is emitted. The snapshot reads text files up to 1000000 bytes and returns nil otherwise.
side_effects: A file read for a write; one provider event
failure_cases: Missing id or name: nothing.
requirements.windows_path: relativePath has the same prefix-stripping caveat as PR-PROVCLI-062. Note the detail here is PRETTY-printed, not compact as in the other providers.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over every name group plus an mcp__ name and an unknown one

requirements.title: Pi reads a declined tool result out of the gate's own block-reason prefix
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiCLI.swift:213 - return { block: true, reason: "The user declined this " + ... }
requirements.preconditions: A tool_execution_end line with a call id.
requirements.expected_result: The output is the text of result.content. isError is message.isError or result.isError being exactly true. The status is .completed when there was no error; otherwise .declined when the output STARTS WITH the literal prefix "The user declined this", and .failed when it does not. The exit code is result.details.exitCode. The edits come from editDiff when both a name and arguments were recorded. One .toolUpdated is emitted with a nil output when the text is empty. This is an ORDERING DEPENDENCY between two files: the prefix here is exactly what the extension's block reason produces, so the two must change together.
failure_cases: An error whose text does not start with that prefix reads as failed, not declined.
requirements.windows_path: The prefix comparison is ordinal. Because the extension text and this comparison must agree byte for byte, any translation or rewording of the shipped TypeScript would silently turn every decline into a failure.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture driving a real decline end to end and asserting the row reads declined

requirements.title: Pi builds a whole-file unified diff for edits and writes, through a no-op relativization
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiSession.swift:468-494 - editDiff and unifiedDiff with the doc comment
requirements.expected_result: For a tool named exactly "edit": a string args.path is required, and the diff is built from args.oldText and args.newText, each defaulting to the empty string. For "write": a string args.path and a string args.content are required, and the old side is the recorded snapshot, REMOVED as it is consumed, defaulting to the empty string. Any other name returns nil. The diff is a header of "--- a/<path>" and "+++ b/<path>" on two lines, then EVERY non-empty line of the old text prefixed with "-", then EVERY non-empty line of the new text prefixed with "+", all joined by single newlines - not a real unified diff with hunks. The additions and deletions come from diffStats. The path is passed through `path.hasPrefix("/") ? path : path`, whose two branches are IDENTICAL, so the ternary is a no-op and the path is NEVER made relative; the FileEdit therefore carries the absolute path.
failure_cases: A missing path or content yields no edits.
requirements.windows_path: The no-op ternary means Pi's file rows show ABSOLUTE paths where the other providers show relative ones, and on Windows those will be drive-letter paths inside a diff header that looks like a POSIX one. This is an upstream defect and is reproduced, not repaired.
requirements.verification_method: unit test asserting the absolute path survives into the diff header
requirements.upstream_defect: provider-argv-and-handshakes.md section 10 item 6 (unifiedDiff's no-op ternary; paths are never relativized)

requirements.title: Pi finishes a turn by publishing a plan in plan mode and choosing one of three statuses

A .planCompleted with id "<launchID>-plan-<turnCounter>" and the last reply text is emitted ONLY when ALL of: the stored interaction mode is .plan, there is no error, the turn was not interrupted, and the last reply is not blank. Then: interruptRequested -> .turnCompleted(.interrupted, nil); else an error -> .turnCompleted(.failed, error); else .turnCompleted(.completed, nil). interruptRequested is reset last.
failure_cases: A plan-mode turn that errored publishes no plan.

requirements.title: Pi dispatches eight extension UI methods across six behaviours, silently ignoring four
requirements.expected_result: The id is message.id or message.requestId; a request with neither, or with no string "method", is ignored. The params are message.params or the message itself. "select" goes to the gate handler. "confirm" records the method and emits a .question whose header is the literal "Pi", whose prompt is params.title (defaulting to the literal "Pi") and params.message joined by a newline with empties dropped, and whose choices are exactly "Yes" then "No", with allowsMultiple false, allowsOther false and isSecret false. "input" and "editor" record their own method and emit a .question with header "Pi", prompt params.title or "Pi", NO choices, allowsOther TRUE and isSecret false. "notify" emits a notice whose level is "warning" -> .warning, "error" -> .error, anything else -> .info, with params.message or the literal "Pi sent a notification." The four names "setStatus", "setWidget", "setTitle" and "set_editor_text" share one label that does NOTHING. Any other method also does nothing.

When both succeed, the payload's fields are "kind", "toolName", "toolCallId" and "input", as the extension wrote them.

requirements.title: Pi auto-allows a gate request whose kind already holds a session grant

When the session grants already contain that EXACT string, a reply {"type":"extension_ui_response","id":<id>,"value":"Allow"} is written at once - the plain "Allow", not "Allow for session" - and no prompt is shown and no event emitted. The grant keys stored by resolveApproval are exactly "command", "fileChange" and "tool", which match the kinds the extension emits.

requirements.title: Pi gate approvals map three kinds to three row shapes and always offer the same three options
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiSession.swift:607-636 - the kind mapping, the title and detail switch, the three options and the emitted approval
requirements.preconditions: A gate request with no matching session grant.
requirements.expected_result: The tool name is payload.toolName or the literal "tool". The kind is .command for the string "command", .fileChange for "fileChange" and .tool for everything else. The row: .command -> title the unwrapped input.command or the tool name, detail the RAW input.command; .fileChange -> title the relative input.path or the tool name, detail the RAW input.path; .tool and the rest -> title the tool name, detail the PRETTY-printed input unless it is null or compacts to "{}". The options are ALWAYS exactly three, in this order: "allow"/"Approve"/.approve, "always"/"Approve for session"/.approveAlways, "deny"/"Decline"/.decline. The toolItemID is payload.toolCallId. The request is stored as pending under the extension request id and emitted as .approval.
side_effects: One provider event; one pending entry
failure_cases: none
requirements.cancellation: A stop leaves the extension waiting; there is no cancellation reply path.
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over all three kinds

requirements.title: Pi's close path ends an active turn, then reports an exit with the status and the stderr tail
requirements.expected_result: The stderr tail is taken FIRST, then the process reference cleared. When a turn was active, it is cleared and .turnCompleted is emitted with .interrupted when interruptRequested, else .failed, carrying the tail as the error when it is non-empty and nil when it is empty. Then, when the session was stopped, the method returns. Otherwise started becomes false and: an exit status of exactly 0 emits .exited(error: nil); any other status emits .exited with "Pi exited with status <status>" plus, when the tail is non-empty, a newline and the tail.
failure_cases: A crash mid-turn reports the turn failed and then the session exited.
requirements.cancellation: A stop suppresses the exit notice but NOT the turn completion, because the turn branch runs before the stopped guard.
requirements.windows_path: The exit status appears verbatim in user-visible text, so a Windows termination code will be shown; the source formats it as a signed integer. The tail comes from the bounded stderr collector (PA-0008).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test over a zero exit, a non-zero exit and a stop mid-turn

requirements.title: Pi reports itself running only when started, not stopped and holding a live process
requirements.action: The thread asks whether the session is running.
requirements.expected_result: All three must hold: started is true, stopped is false, and the process exists and reports itself running. This is stricter than Command Code, which asks only the two flags, and stricter than Claude, which asks only the process.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: The process must report not-running promptly after it exits, or send() will attempt a write to a dead pipe.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over each of the three false cases

requirements.title: The Pi gate extension is written as droppy-gate.ts only when its bytes change
requirements.expected_result: The support directory is created with intermediate directories. The file is named exactly "droppy-gate.ts". Its UTF-8 bytes are compared against whatever is on disk and written atomically ONLY when they differ, so a new build's extension replaces the old one. The URL is returned; a write failure propagates.

requirements.verification_method: restart test asserting the file is not rewritten when unchanged

requirements.title: The Pi extension registers MCP tools from the bridge with a middle-dot label and swallows every error
requirements.expected_result: When the environment key is set the bridge module is imported and AWAITED. For each tool it lists, pi.registerTool is called with name "mcp__" + server + "__" + name, label server + " · " + name (space, U+00B7, space), the tool's description, parameters Type.Unsafe(tool.inputSchema), and an execute function returning { content: [{ type: "text", text }], details: {} }. Any error anywhere in that block is caught and logged to stderr as "droppy mcp: " plus the error's message (or its string form for a non-Error) and otherwise SWALLOWED. Unlike the Command Code mod, this import IS awaited, so tools are registered before the agent runs.
side_effects: Tools registered in the CLI; stderr output on failure
failure_cases: A failing bridge leaves the MCP tools absent, with only a stderr line.
requirements.windows_path: The bridge path is handed to a dynamic import; whether a Windows path works directly or needs a file URL must be probed against the real CLI.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test with a stand-in bridge, and a Windows import-form probe

requirements.title: The Pi extension appends up to three system-prompt segments before the agent starts
requirements.preconditions: The agent is about to start a turn.
requirements.expected_result: The gate is read from the file named by DROPPY_CODE_PI_GATE, or the empty string; ANY throw, including a missing file or malformed JSON, yields an empty object. Three candidate strings are considered IN THIS ORDER: when gate.finalReport is truthy, "Reply with your final report now: no tools, one message."; when gate.interactionMode is exactly "plan", "You are in plan mode: read-only. Do not edit files or run commands that change anything; investigate, then end with the plan as markdown."; when gate.systemPrompt is a string of length greater than zero, that string - a branch that is unreachable in the shipped build. When none applies the hook returns NOTHING and the prompt is untouched. Otherwise the hook returns a system prompt of the event's own prompt, two newlines, and the candidates joined by two newlines.
side_effects: The agent's system prompt is extended
failure_cases: An unreadable gate file silently means no segments are appended, so a plan-mode turn would not be told it is read-only. The tool_call hook's own plan check is what still blocks the tools.
requirements.windows_path: The gate path comes from the environment and is read with a plain filesystem read.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture driving the real extension text with each gate shape

requirements.title: The Pi extension's tool_call hook applies an eight-step decision ladder in a fixed order
requirements.preconditions: A tool is about to run.
requirements.expected_result: The gate is re-read on EVERY call. The ladder, in this exact order: (1) gate.finalReport truthy blocks with reason "Final report: no tools"; (2) a tool name in the four-element read-only set read, grep, find, ls is ALLOWED, even in plan mode and even during a final report - note step 1 is tested before this, so a final report blocks even a read; (3) gate.interactionMode exactly "plan" blocks with reason "Plan mode is read-only"; (4) gate.runtimeMode exactly "fullAccess" allows; (5) the kind is computed as "command" for the tool name "bash", "fileChange" for "edit" or "write", and "tool" otherwise; (6) a fileChange under runtimeMode "autoAcceptEdits" or "auto" allows; (7) a command under runtimeMode "auto" whose input.command is read-only allows; (8) otherwise the user is asked. All the mode comparisons are against the camelCase raw values.
failure_cases: An unreadable gate yields an empty object, so every step falls through to asking the user - the safe answer.
requirements.windows_path: The camelCase mode strings are the on-disk contract described in PR-PROVCLI-277.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture driving the real extension text through every rung of the ladder

requirements.title: The Pi extension classifies a shell command as read-only by splitting on four separators and checking every segment
requirements.expected_result: The command is coerced to a string (a nullish value becomes the empty string) and split on the regular expression matching "&&", "||", ";" or "|". EVERY segment must qualify. A segment is trimmed and split on whitespace with empties dropped; a segment with NO words qualifies. A segment whose first word is exactly "git" qualifies only when it has a second word in the six-element set status, diff, log, show, branch, blame. Otherwise the first word must be in the eighteen-element set, in source order: ls, cat, head, tail, grep, rg, find, wc, pwd, echo, which, stat, file, du, tree, sort, uniq, diff. Note this list has no path handling, so a command written as "/bin/ls" does NOT qualify.
failure_cases: Anything not provably read-only is asked, which is the safe answer.
requirements.windows_path: These are Unix tool names, but the classifier runs on the COMMAND TEXT THE MODEL PRODUCED inside the CLI, so the list is a product constant and is copied verbatim. Whether a Windows-hosted Pi produces Windows command text instead is UNK-0005 and is not guessed; if it does, this classifier simply asks more often, which is safe.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture driving the real extension text over a pipeline, a git subcommand, an unknown binary and an empty segment

requirements.title: The Pi extension truncates long string inputs at twenty thousand characters before asking
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiCLI.swift:206-209 - the input copy with the 20000-character slice
requirements.preconditions: The hook has decided to ask.
requirements.expected_result: A fresh object is built from the event's input (or an empty object): every value that is a string LONGER than 20000 characters is replaced by its first 20000 characters; every other value is copied unchanged, including nested objects, which are NOT recursed into. Only top-level string values are truncated.
failure_cases: A large nested object still reaches the select title in full.
requirements.windows_path: The measure is JavaScript string length, which counts UTF-16 code units, so a slice can split a surrogate pair; that is the shipped behavior and is reproduced.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture with a 25000-character string input

requirements.title: The Pi extension asks over a select whose title is a droppy-gate prefix and a JSON payload
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiCLI.swift:210-213 - the payload, the select call and the block reason
requirements.preconditions: The ladder reached the ask step.
requirements.expected_result: The payload is { kind, toolName, toolCallId, input } in that written order. The select title is the literal "droppy-gate " - with a trailing space - followed by JSON.stringify of that payload. The options array is exactly ["Allow", "Allow for session", "Deny"] in that order. An answer of exactly "Allow" or exactly "Allow for session" returns undefined, allowing the call. Anything else, including a cancellation, blocks with the reason "The user declined this " followed by "command" for a command kind, "file change" for a fileChange kind and "tool call" otherwise.

requirements.title: Pi's config directory honours PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR and otherwise sits under the home directory
requirements.expected_result: When PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR is set and non-empty, that path is used verbatim as a directory URL. Otherwise the home is environment["HOME"] when non-empty, else LoginEnvironment.homeDirectory, and the directory is that home joined with the literal segment ".pi/agent".

requirements.title: Pi auth status reports the sorted provider names from auth.json, else any of eight environment keys
requirements.action: Settings reads the Pi sign-in state.

requirements.title: Pi reads Codex usage with an account id taken from the token's own claim
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiPlanLimits.swift:8,:59-79 - codexUsageURL and readCodex with the comment at :64
requirements.preconditions: A live openai-codex or openai OAuth token.

When an account id can be extracted and is non-empty, the header "ChatGPT-Account-Id" carries it. The account id comes from the token's SECOND dot-separated part decoded as base64url: hyphens become plus, underscores become slash, and the string is padded with equals signs to a multiple of four; the decoded JSON's field at the path "https://api.openai.com/auth" then "chatgpt_account_id" is the id. A token with fewer than two parts, or one that fails to decode or parse, yields no id and the header is omitted. Anything but HTTP 200, or an unparseable body, yields nil. The rate limit object is json.rate_limit, else the whole body. Two windows are built from "primary_window" and "secondary_window"; with none, nil. The plan name is json.plan_type mapped through PlanLimitsReader.codexPlanName and prefixed "Codex ", or the bare literal "Codex".

failure_cases: A malformed token simply omits the header, which may make the endpoint answer for the wrong scope or refuse.
requirements.windows_path: Base64 decoding must be strict about the padding rule described; a decoder that rejects unpadded input would break the header. No credential is ever written anywhere.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over a token with and without the claim, plus a recorded usage response

requirements.title: Antigravity normalizes the model and effort into at most two flags, suppressing effort for any claude slug
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/AntigravitySession.swift:84-87 - the normalize call and the two conditional flags
requirements.preconditions: A model and an effort, either possibly nil.
requirements.expected_result: A nil or EMPTY model returns (nil, nil), so NEITHER --model nor --effort is passed whatever the effort setting. Otherwise the slug is parsed: a trailing "-high", "-medium" or "-low" is stripped, TESTED IN THAT ORDER, and the matching " (High)", " (Medium)" or " (Low)" suffix stripped from the display name, yielding a base slug and a parsed effort. A base slug CONTAINING the substring "claude" returns (baseSlug, nil), so such a model gets --model and NO --effort. Otherwise the effort is resolved in this precedence: the explicit effort argument; then the effort parsed out of the slug suffix; then a default of "medium" for the exact slug "gpt-oss-120b" and "high" for everything else. Then two hard overrides are applied AFTER the default: the exact slug "gemini-3.1-pro" with effort "medium" becomes "high"; the exact slug "gpt-oss-120b" is ALWAYS forced to "medium", overriding even an explicit high or low. The resulting model appends "--model" and its value when non-empty; the resulting effort appends "--effort" and its value when non-empty. The only literal model identifiers compared are the substring "claude" and the exact slugs "gemini-3.1-pro" and "gpt-oss-120b". The CLI accepts exactly three efforts: low, medium, high.
failure_cases: A user's chosen effort can be silently overridden by the two hard rules.
requirements.windows_path: The substring and equality tests are ordinal.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over an empty model, a claude slug, gpt-oss-120b with an explicit high, gemini-3.1-pro with medium, and a slug carrying a -low suffix

requirements.title: Antigravity's per-turn mode and model state is half applied and half discarded
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/AntigravitySession.swift:88 - start() reads configuration.runtimeMode and configuration.interactionMode, NOT the stored properties
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/AntigravitySession.swift:85-87 - start() reads the STORED model and effort
requirements.preconditions: A live session whose modes or model change between turns.

requirements.expected_result: send(_:) writes runtimeMode, interactionMode, model and effort. But start() builds its mode flags from configuration.runtimeMode and configuration.interactionMode - the LAUNCH-TIME values - while building its model and effort flags from the STORED model and effort. The consequence, which is the behavior to reproduce: a mid-thread mode or Plan/Build change CANNOT reach agy at all, and even a relaunch uses the ORIGINAL modes while picking up the UPDATED model and effort. Half the per-turn state is applied and half discarded. The stored runtimeMode and interactionMode are proven write-only. Reproduce the behavior, not the intent: carry the properties if porting literally, but do NOT wire them up.

requirements.windows_path: None. Contrast Pi, where the same switch DOES take effect because the gate file is rewritten every turn (PR-PROVCLI-277). Antigravity and the ACP providers require a process restart for a mode change; Claude, Codex, Copilot outside the Auto boundary, Pi and Command Code apply live (port_impacts.md entry 23).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test changing the runtime mode between turns and asserting the argv of a relaunch is unchanged in its mode flags but updated in its model flag
requirements.upstream_defect: upstream_defects.md entry 2 (runtimeMode and interactionMode are write-only; a mid-thread mode change cannot reach agy)

requirements.title: Antigravity start resolves only on an init event carrying a non-empty conversation id

The process is created with the default line framing, the working directory and configuration.environment UNMODIFIED - this file writes no environment key. isStopping is cleared so a previous interrupt does not suppress this launch's exit reporting. try process.start() propagates a launch failure. A read task consumes messages and calls didClose when the stream ends. start() then suspends on a continuation that is resolved by the FIRST inbound line whose "event" is exactly "init" AND whose "conversation_id" is a non-empty string; that id is stored, the continuation resumed with it, and .sessionReady emitted. An init with an empty or missing id is IGNORED and the wait continues.

requirements.title: Antigravity interrupt sets the stopping flag before killing, so the chat does not read an unexpected exit
requirements.expected_result: With no active turn nothing happens. Otherwise interruptRequested is set, THEN isStopping is set, THEN the process is terminated. The ordering matters: without isStopping, didClose would follow the interrupted turn with an .exited event and the chat would read that Antigravity stopped unexpectedly every time the user stopped a turn. There is NO interrupt message, because the stream has none; stopping the process ends the turn and the conversation persists server-side for the next turn's --conversation resume. start() clears isStopping again for the next launch.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: TerminateProcess behaves like SIGKILL, which is acceptable because the source already relies only on server-side persistence and nothing is flushed on the signal. The FLAG-BEFORE-KILL ORDERING must be preserved so the chat does not read an unexpected exit (port_impacts.md entry 24).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test asserting no .exited event follows an interrupt

requirements.title: Antigravity streams reply text under a step-index-keyed id and reports per-step context usage
requirements.expected_result: The step index is step.step_index or zero. When step.usage yields a context usage it is emitted as .usage FIRST; that usage is (input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + output_tokens), each defaulting to zero, nil when the sum is not greater than zero, and its window is ALWAYS nil - result totals are the session's cumulative spend and say nothing about the window. Then, when step.text_delta is a non-empty string, streamedText is set and .messageDelta is emitted with id "agy-<launchID>-message-<step_index>", where launchID is the first eight characters of a fresh uppercase UUID computed once per session. The namespacing exists because step_index counts up within one process but a resumed conversation starts over, and a repeated id would stream a new turn's text into an old entry.

requirements.title: Antigravity announces a tool step once, snapshotting a file when an edit goes active

Then, when the state was "ACTIVE", the handler RETURNS - so an active step only ever opens the row. A step that surfaces only as finished therefore still gets a proper row rather than a bare "Tool". The snapshot reads text files up to 1000000 bytes and yields nil otherwise, so a write shows as a whole-file addition.

requirements.verification_method: unit test over an ACTIVE-then-DONE pair and a DONE-only step

requirements.preconditions: A tool step that is not in its opening ACTIVE state.
requirements.expected_result: When the state is exactly "ERROR", OR the state is exactly "DONE" and tool_info.error.message is present, the message is that error or the literal "The tool failed.", and the status is .declined when isDenied matches it and .failed when it does not; .toolUpdated is emitted with that output, that status and the finished edits. Errors ride on the error field as well as an ERROR state, so either ends the call as a failure. Otherwise, when the state is exactly "DONE", the status is .completed, the output is tool_info.output when it is a non-empty string, and the finished edits are attached. isDenied lowercases the message and matches exactly three substrings: "permission check failed", "denied permission", "permission denied" - the soft-deny wording headless runs use when a rule blocks a tool. finishEdit returns nil unless a snapshot was recorded AND a path is present, in which case it re-reads the file and returns one path-only FileEdit when nothing changed, or one FileEdit carrying the before and after text when it did.
side_effects: A file read on completion; one provider event
failure_cases: Any other state emits nothing at all.
requirements.windows_path: The lowercased substring tests must be invariant.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over ERROR, DONE with an error, DONE clean, and a denied message

requirements.title: Antigravity converts a cumulative session total into per-turn spend, seeding a resumed conversation's baseline uncharged
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/AntigravitySession.swift:290-319 - handleResult's usage block with the comment at :294-301
requirements.expected_result: turnActive becomes false and both editSnapshots and startedTools are cleared FIRST. Then, when result.usage exists and is not JSON null: used is usage.total_tokens, or, when absent, (usage.input_tokens + usage.output_tokens) each defaulting to zero. When used is greater than zero: if the baseline is known, the spend tracker converts the cumulative total into a delta and, when that delta is positive, records it in TokenLedger and emits .tokenSpend with provider .antigravity, that delta as the total and the stored model; if the baseline is NOT known, the tracker's baseline is SEEDED with the total, the flag set, and NOTHING is charged. Totals are cumulative over the session per the headless docs; a conversation resumed with --conversation reports a total that already holds its history and the protocol does not say how much, so the first total is left uncounted rather than charged as new spend or reported as zero. The context meter is fed per step instead.
side_effects: A TokenLedger write; at most one provider event
failure_cases: Zero usage records nothing.
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over a fresh conversation's first two results and a resumed conversation's first result

requirements.title: Antigravity shows a result-only reply, warns about held-back actions and adopts a conversation id
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/AntigravitySession.swift:320-338 - the response, denied_actions and conversation_id blocks
requirements.expected_result: When NOTHING streamed this turn and result.response is a string that is not blank, .messageCompleted is emitted with id "agy-<launchID>-result-<an eight-character UUID prefix>" and that text - resumed conversations can answer in the result alone. streamedText is then reset. The denied list is, per entry of result.denied_actions, its "display_name" else its "action". When that list is non-empty a WARNING notice is emitted reading "Antigravity held back <names> without prompting. Use Full access or add an allow rule in the CLI's settings." where names is the list joined by ", ". When result.conversation_id is a non-empty string it replaces the stored id and .sessionReady is emitted.
requirements.persistence: The conversation id is the thread's persisted resume id.
failure_cases: A blank response draws nothing.
requirements.windows_path: The notice names the CLI's settings, not the app's; the wording is source text.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over a streamed turn, a result-only turn and a turn with denied actions

requirements.title: Antigravity ends a turn on one of five status branches, testing denied WAITING first
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/AntigravitySession.swift:339-360 - the status switch with the comments at :344-346 and :349-350
requirements.expected_result: When interruptRequested is set, the turn is .interrupted with a nil error and the status is not consulted at all. Otherwise result.status is matched: "WAITING" WITH A NON-EMPTY denied list, tested FIRST, gives .failed with the error "Antigravity held back <names> waiting for a permission it could not ask for. Use Full access for this chat." where names is the denied list joined by ", " - reported as a failure so a head's lead hears it was starved of permissions rather than reading a clean completion. "SUCCESS" or "WAITING" (without denials) gives .completed with a nil error; WAITING means the agent stopped to ask something it cannot ask headless, the turn is over and the reply says what it needs. "CANCELED" or "INTERRUPTED" gives .interrupted. Anything else, including a missing status, gives .failed with result.error when it is a non-empty string and the literal "Antigravity stopped before finishing." otherwise. interruptRequested is reset last.
failure_cases: Every branch above.
requirements.cancellation: An interrupt short-circuits the whole switch.
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over all five branches including WAITING with and without denials

requirements.title: Antigravity's close path fails a waiting start, ends an active turn and reports an exit only when not stopping
requirements.expected_result: When start() is still waiting, its continuation is cleared and resumed by throwing ProviderError.failed with the auth hint when one applies, else the last lines of the stderr tail, else the literal "Antigravity exited." When a turn was active, it is cleared and .turnCompleted is emitted: .interrupted with a nil error when interruptRequested, otherwise .failed with the auth hint, else the tail's last lines, else "Antigravity exited."; interruptRequested is then reset. Finally, only when isStopping is false, .exited(error: <the tail's last lines>) is emitted. The auth hint fires when the LOWERCASED tail contains "authentication required", OR "not signed in", OR "unauthenticated", OR both "login" AND "agy"; it is the verbatim string "Antigravity is not signed in. Run `agy` once in Terminal to sign in."
failure_cases: Every branch above.
requirements.cancellation: A stop or an interrupt suppresses the exit notice but NOT the turn completion.
requirements.windows_path: The substring tests must be invariant-lowercased. The hint's Terminal wording reads as macOS text; changing it is a product decision. The tail comes from the bounded stderr collector (PA-0008).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test over a crash during start, a crash mid-turn, an interrupt and a stop

requirements.title: Antigravity lists models from a TSV, collapsing effort variants into one row per base slug
requirements.action: The registry loads the Antigravity catalog.
requirements.expected_result: Two Shell.run calls are made CONCURRENTLY, each with a 30 second timeout: ["models"] and ["-p", "/model", "--output-format", "json"]. The current model id is read from the second's stdout parsed as JSON at the path command.data.id. When the first produced no decodable stdout, ShellError("`agy models` produced no output.") is thrown verbatim. Otherwise the ANSI-stripped text is split into lines; each is trimmed, empties skipped, and split on a TAB with at most one split. The first part must satisfy isSlug - a leading letter or number, then only letters, numbers, hyphen, underscore and period, and no spaces - or the line is skipped, which is how progress output on stderr and any header line is excluded. The name is the second part when present and non-empty, else the slug. The row is parsed into a base slug, base name and effort. A row is current when its slug equals the current id, OR its base slug equals it, OR the current id STARTS WITH its base slug. Rows are grouped by base slug in FIRST-SEEN order: the first occurrence sets the name, the efforts list (one entry when the row carried an effort, empty otherwise) and the current flag; later occurrences append a new effort if it is not already there and set the current flag if that row is current. Each group becomes a ModelOption whose efforts are the intersection with ["low", "medium", "high"] IN THAT ORDER, whose default effort is "high" when present and otherwise the LAST of the sorted efforts, and whose isDefault is the group's flag. An empty list throws ShellError("`agy models` listed no models.") verbatim. When NO row is marked default, the FIRST row is rewritten to be the default.
failure_cases: The two exact messages above.
requirements.windows_path: ANSI stripping is load-bearing on Windows. The TSV parse depends on the CLI emitting a real tab; a Windows console that pads with spaces instead would drop every row, so the real output must be captured on Windows before this is called verified.
requirements.verification_method: unit test against a captured `agy models` output, plus a Windows capture comparison

requirements.title: Antigravity auth status runs agy models and reads three signals, defaulting to the exit status
requirements.action: Settings reads the Antigravity sign-in state.
requirements.expected_result: Shell.run(executable, ["models"], environment:, timeout: 20) runs - a 20 second timeout, shorter than every other Antigravity call. A throw returns .unknown. ANSI is stripped from stdout plus stderr. The rows are the lines whose first tab-separated field satisfies isSlug. When the run SUCCEEDED and there is at least one row, .signedIn(nil) is returned. Otherwise, when the lowercased text contains "authentication required", "not signed in", "unauthenticated", "sign in" or "login" - five substrings, two more than the didClose hint uses - .signedOut is returned. Otherwise the result is .signedIn(nil) when the run succeeded and .unknown when it did not. Antigravity never reports an account NAME.
failure_cases: An unreachable CLI: .unknown.
requirements.windows_path: ANSI stripping and invariant lowercasing are both load-bearing.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over a successful listing, a sign-in message and an unclassifiable failure

requirements.title: Antigravity reads plan limits from two zero-token headless calls and never reports a plan name
requirements.action: The usage panel reads Antigravity's limits.
requirements.expected_result: Two Shell.run calls are made CONCURRENTLY, each with a 30 second timeout: ["-p", "/usage", "--output-format", "json"] and ["-p", "/credits", "--output-format", "json"]. Both are zero-token headless calls, so reading limits never spends quota itself. Each stdout is decoded and parsed as JSON; a failure at any step simply contributes nothing. The usage windows come from parseUsage(json.command.data, fallback: json.response), appended first; the credits window, when parseCredits(json.command.data, fallback: json.response) yields one, is appended last. With NO windows at all the result is nil; otherwise a PlanLimits whose planName is ALWAYS NIL - Antigravity never reports a plan name, unlike Codex, Copilot and Command Code.
requirements.persistence: The registry persists the plan limits.
failure_cases: Both calls failing yields nil.
requirements.windows_path: None beyond process spawning.
requirements.verification_method: unit test against recorded envelopes for both routes

requirements.title: Antigravity usage windows take the complement of a remaining fraction, with a tab-separated text fallback
requirements.expected_result: For each group in data.groups: the group name is group.name or the literal "Models". For each bucket in group.buckets, a double "remaining_fraction" is required or the bucket is skipped. The window id is bucket.id, or "<groupName>-<the number of windows so far>". The title is "<groupName> · <bucket.name or the literal "Limit">" - space, U+00B7, space. The percent is max(0, min(100, (1 - remaining) * 100)), clamped at BOTH ends. resetsAt is bucket.reset_time parsed by a default ISO8601DateFormatter. When the structured pass produced NO windows and a fallback response string exists, the text parser runs instead: each line is split on TABS and needs at least three parts; the third part has its percent sign removed and must parse as a double, which is what REMAINS; the reset is the fourth part parsed as ISO 8601 when there are at least four; the id is "usage-<the number of windows so far>"; the title is "<first part> · <second part>"; and the percent is max(0, min(100, 100 - remaining)).
requirements.persistence: Part of the persisted plan limits.
failure_cases: A bucket without a remaining fraction is skipped.
requirements.windows_path: The ISO 8601 parsing must be culture-invariant. The middle dot must survive as UTF-8.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over the structured envelope and the text fallback

requirements.title: Antigravity's credit window is binary: zero percent while any credits remain, a hundred when none do
requirements.expected_result: When data.remaining_credits is an Int, the window is returned at once with id the literal "ai-credits", title "AI credits · <remaining> remaining" - space, U+00B7, space - percent 0 when remaining is greater than zero and 100 otherwise, and no reset time. Otherwise, when a fallback response string exists, each line is split on tabs and needs at least two parts whose FIRST part case-insensitively contains "credit" and whose SECOND part parses as an Int; the FIRST such line yields the same window shape. With neither, nil. Recorded upstream oddity: the function declares a `fallback response:` parameter, but the structured branch returns before consulting it, so the fallback only runs when remaining_credits is absent - which is correct behavior, but the parameter is never used on the structured path. Transcribe faithfully rather than simplifying the signature.
requirements.persistence: Part of the persisted plan limits.
failure_cases: Neither shape: nil, and no credit window appears.
requirements.windows_path: The case-insensitive contains must be invariant.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over the structured shape, the text fallback and neither
requirements.upstream_defect: provider-argv-and-handshakes.md section 10 item 10 (parseCredits declares a fallback parameter its structured branch never consults)

requirements.title: Antigravity maps fifty named tools to seven kinds and everything else to other
requirements.expected_result: The complete table, verbatim. .command, 6 names: run_command, send_command_input, command_status, wait, wait_5_seconds, schedule. .read, 8 names: view_file, view_file_outline, view_code_item, view_content_chunk, read_resource, read_browser_page, capture_browser_screenshot, capture_browser_console_logs. .edit, 6 names: write_to_file, replace_file_content, multi_replace_file_content, sed_file, notebook_edit, notebook_execution. .search, 5 names: list_dir, grep_search, find_by_name, list_resources, list_browser_pages. .web, 20 names: search_web, read_url_content, open_browser_url, browser_click_element, browser_drag_pixel_to_pixel, browser_get_dom, browser_get_network_request, browser_input, browser_list_network_requests, browser_mouse_down, browser_mouse_up, browser_move_mouse, browser_press_key, browser_refresh_page, browser_resize_window, browser_scroll, browser_scroll_dom, browser_select_option, click_browser_pixel, execute_browser_javascript. .agent, 4 names: invoke_subagent, browser_subagent, define_subagent, manage_subagents. .mcp, 1 name: call_mcp_tool. Everything else is .other. Fifty tools are named in total.
failure_cases: An unnamed tool renders as .other.
requirements.windows_path: None. This is a product table and every entry must be transcribed; a dropped name changes which icon and row shape the user sees.
requirements.verification_method: unit test asserting all fifty names map to the stated kind and an unknown name maps to other

requirements.title: Antigravity builds each tool row from ordered parameter key lists, never from the edit content
requirements.preconditions: A tool name and its parameters.
requirements.expected_result: The path is the first non-empty string among these ELEVEN keys IN THIS ORDER: AbsolutePath, TargetFile, NotebookPath, FilePath, File, file, path, Path, DirectoryPath, directory, dir; when found it is made relative to the working directory. Then by kind: .command -> title the unwrapped first of CommandLine, command, Command, else humanize(name). .read -> title the path, else the first of Url, URL, url, else humanize(name); and when a path was found and StartLine is an int, the detail is "L<start>–<end>" with an EN DASH when EndLine is an int greater than start, and "L<start>" otherwise. .edit -> title the path or humanize(name), and when a path was found one path-only FileEdit. .search -> the pattern is the first of Query, query, Pattern, pattern and the folder the first of SearchPath, SearchDirectory, DirectoryPath, Path, path made relative; with a pattern the title is the pattern and the detail the folder, without one the title is the folder or humanize(name). .web -> title the first of Url, URL, url, query, Query, else humanize(name). .agent -> title the first of Task, task, Prompt, prompt, Description, description flattened to 96 characters, else humanize(name). .mcp -> title "<the first of ServerName, server_name, Server, server, or MCP> · <the first of ToolName, tool_name, Tool, tool, or tool>", detail the compact value of Arguments, else arguments, else Input, unless it is null. .other -> title humanize(name), with the compact parameters as the detail ONLY when non-empty, not "{}" and at most 300 characters. humanize splits on underscores and CAPITALIZES ONLY THE FIRST WORD using Swift's capitalized. The stream sends a DISPLAY SUBSET of the parameters and NEVER the edit content, which is why finishEdit snapshots the file before and after instead of reading a diff off the wire.
failure_cases: No recognizable key falls back to the humanized tool name.
requirements.windows_path: relativePath has the same prefix-stripping caveat as PR-PROVCLI-062. The en dash must survive as a non-ASCII character. Note Antigravity's humanize uses `capitalized` on the first word, which lowercases the remaining characters of that word, unlike Command Code's humanize which only uppercases the first character - the two must not be shared.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over every kind and every key list, including a word like "MCP" passed through humanize

ui.element: Approve button on an ordinary tool, command or file-change approval
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area. These adapters emit an ApprovalRequest.Option; the approval card that renders it owns every dimension, inset, radius and spacing. Source for the visual treatment is the chrome and design-token area, not these files.
ui.typography: Not defined in this area; owned by the approval card.
ui.colors: Not defined in this area; the role .approve is what the card uses to pick its treatment, and the role is the only visual signal these files carry.
states: Present on every non-plan approval from Claude, Command Code and Pi, and on Copilot permission prompts
Disabled or removed when the request is withdrawn: Claude on control_cancel_request, Copilot on permission.completed, Codex on serverRequest/resolved, Command Code on tool_hook_blocked or tool_denied
Removed when the turn is stopped
interactions: click - resolves the request with the option id "allow" (Claude, Copilot, Command Code, Pi)
ui.notes: The option id is "allow" in all four providers, but the wire effect differs: Claude sends a behavior object, Copilot a decision kind, Command Code writes a reply FILE and Pi sends the literal string "Allow". Codex uses different ids entirely (see UI-PROVCLI-006 and UI-PROVCLI-009).

ui.element: Approve for session button
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the approval card.
ui.colors: Not defined in this area; the role is .approveAlways.
states: ALWAYS present on Command Code and Pi approvals
CONDITIONAL on Claude: present only when the CLI sent a non-empty permission_suggestions array

CONDITIONAL on Copilot: present only when a session approval can be built for that request kind (shell and write need canOfferSessionApproval true and, for shell, at least one command identifier; url needs a parseable host; mcp and custom-tool need a name; read and memory always qualify; every other kind hides it)
Absent from every plan approval
interactions: click - resolves with the option id "always", which on Claude also sends session-scoped permission suggestions, on Copilot sends an approve-for-session decision, and on Command Code and Pi additionally records a session grant keyed "command", "fileChange" or "tool" so later requests of that kind are auto-allowed
ui.notes: A porter will be tempted to show this button unconditionally because two of the four providers do. Claude and Copilot hide it, and hiding it is the only signal the user gets that the CLI cannot remember that decision.

ui.element: Decline button
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the approval card.
ui.colors: Not defined in this area; the role is .decline.
states: Present on every non-plan approval from Claude, Copilot, Command Code and Pi
Also the label Codex uses in both its decision list and its permissions list
interactions: click - resolves with the option id "deny" on Claude, Copilot, Command Code and Pi, and with "decline" on Codex
ui.notes: The option ID differs between providers ("deny" versus "decline") while the LABEL is identical. Pi resolves by ROLE rather than by id, so an unrecognized id there also declines.

ui.element: Implement plan button
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the plan card.
ui.colors: Not defined in this area; the role is .approve.
states: Present on Claude's ExitPlanMode approval and Copilot's exitPlanMode.request approval
Never accompanied by a session option
interactions: click - option id "allow"; on Claude this also emits a mode change to build and re-sends the permission mode, and on Copilot it answers with approved true and selectedAction "interactive" and emits a mode change to build
ui.notes: The approval's title is "Implement this plan" while the button reads "Implement plan" - the two strings differ and both are verbatim.

ui.element: Keep planning button
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the plan card.
ui.colors: Not defined in this area; the role is .decline.
states: Present on Claude's and Copilot's plan approvals
interactions: click - option id "deny"; Claude answers with the message "The user wants to keep planning. Wait for their feedback before changing anything." and Copilot answers approved false with that same sentence as its feedback
ui.notes: The same sentence is sent by two providers through two different wire shapes; it must stay identical in both.

ui.screen: Chat transcript, tool approval card (Codex only)
ui.element: Stop turn button
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the approval card.
ui.colors: Not defined in this area; the role is .cancel, which is unique to this option.
states: Present whenever the Codex server offers the decision name "cancel", which is also in the default four-element list used when the server offers none
Sorted LAST, after approve, approveAlways and decline
interactions: click - option id "cancel"; the stored server payload for that name is echoed back as the decision
ui.notes: This is the only approval option in the area with the .cancel role, and the only one that ends the whole turn rather than one call. The sort order [.approve, .approveAlways, .decline, .cancel] is what puts it last.

ui.screen: Chat transcript, command approval card (Codex only)
ui.element: Always allow button
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the approval card.
ui.colors: Not defined in this area; the role is .approveAlways, so it sorts beside "Approve for session".
states: Present ONLY on a command approval (command: true) whose available decisions include a non-string decision carrying the key "acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment"
Never present on file-change or permission approvals
interactions: click - option id "amend"; the whole decision object is echoed back, which amends the CLI's exec policy
ui.notes: Two .approveAlways options can appear together - "Approve for session" and "Always allow" - and the sort is by role only, so their relative order is whatever the server listed. A stable sort is required to reproduce that.

ui.screen: Chat transcript, permissions approval card (Codex only)
ui.element: Allow once button
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the approval card.
ui.colors: Not defined in this area; the role is .approve.
states: Present on every item/permissions/requestApproval, as one of a FIXED three-option list that is never filtered
interactions: click - option id "turn"; answers with the originally requested permission object and scope "turn"
ui.notes: Note the wording differs from every other approve button in the area, which read "Approve". This card is the only place "Allow once" appears.

ui.screen: Chat transcript, permissions approval card (Codex only)
ui.element: Allow for session button
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the approval card.
ui.colors: Not defined in this area; the role is .approveAlways.

interactions: click - option id "session"; answers with the originally requested permission object and scope "session"
ui.notes: "Allow for session" (Codex permissions) and "Approve for session" (everywhere else) are two DIFFERENT strings and must not be unified.

ui.element: Yes choice
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the question sheet.
states: Present on a Pi extension_ui_request whose method is exactly "confirm", always as the first of exactly two choices
allowsOther is false, so no free-text field appears
interactions: click - answered as confirmed true, because the reply sets "confirmed" to whether the first selected text is exactly "Yes"

ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the question sheet.
states: Present on a Pi confirm question as the second of exactly two choices
interactions: click - answered as confirmed false, since the text is not exactly "Yes"
ui.notes: Dismissing the sheet without choosing sends "cancelled": true instead, which is a third outcome the two buttons cannot express.

ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the question sheet.

The prompt beneath it is params.title for input and editor, defaulting to the literal "Pi" as well, so a title-less input shows "Pi" twice

ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the approval card.

ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the plan card.

ui.notes: "Implement this plan" (title) and "Implement plan" (button) differ by one word; both are verbatim and neither may be normalized to the other.

ui.screen: Chat transcript, permissions approval card (Codex only)

ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the approval card.

Otherwise the title is the applicable parts joined by " · " (space, U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT, space): "Write to <paths joined by comma-space>" when fileSystem.write is non-empty; "Read <paths joined by comma-space>" when fileSystem.read is non-empty; "Network access" when network.enabled is true
ui.notes: The path lists are the server's own strings and are NOT made relative to the working directory.

ui.screen: Chat transcript, permission approval card (Copilot only)
ui.element: Titles for the nine Copilot permission kinds
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the approval card.
states: shell: the unwrapped full command, or the literal "Command"
write: the relative resolved path, or fileName, or the literal "file"
read: "Read " followed by that same path fallback chain
url: "Fetch " followed by the url, or the literal "a URL"
mcp: "<serverName or MCP> · <toolTitle or toolName or tool>"

any other kind: the kind name with hyphens and underscores replaced by spaces and the first character uppercased, or that treatment of the literal "action" when no kind is given

ui.element: Auto model row
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the model picker.
states: ALWAYS index 0 of the Copilot catalog, prepended before the server's models are read, so it survives even when every server model is filtered out as disabled
Marked as the default row
Carries no efforts, so the effort slider is absent while it is selected
interactions: click - selects the model id "auto", which Copilot resolves per request
ui.notes: Its detail line is the verbatim "Copilot picks the model for each request". A catalog equal to exactly this one row is treated by the registry as 'not yet loaded', so the row doubles as a sentinel and its fields must not drift.

ui.element: Model row detail for a metered or unconfigured model
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the model picker.
states: A billing multiplier shows "<n>× premium requests" with an integer when the multiplier is whole, and the fractional value otherwise; the symbol is U+00D7 MULTIPLICATION SIGN, never the letter x
A policy state of exactly "unconfigured" adds the verbatim "Enable it in your GitHub Copilot settings first" with NO trailing period
Both together are joined by " · " (space, U+00B7, space)
Neither present leaves the detail nil and the row shows no second line

ui.element: The nine seed model rows shown before a live catalog is fetched
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the model picker.
states: Shown in this exact order with these exact names and details: "Claude Sonnet 5" / "Anthropic · best combo of speed & intelligence" (the default row); "Claude Fable 5.1" / "Anthropic · most capable for demanding reasoning & long-horizon agents"; "Claude Opus 5" / "Anthropic · most intelligent Opus for agents and coding"; "GPT-6 Astra" / "OpenAI · most capable OpenAI model for demanding reasoning & agents"; "GPT-5.6 Sol" / "OpenAI · latest frontier model for general complex work"; "Gemini 3.8 Flash" / "Google · newest Gemini Flash, improved core reasoning"; "DeepSeek V4 Flash" / "Open Source · fast hybrid-attention reasoning"; "Kimi K3" / "Open Source · long-horizon coding & knowledge work with 1M context"; "GLM 5.3" / "Open Source · frontier coding with emergent cyber capabilities"
Only the first row is marked default
Replaced wholesale once a live catalog is fetched
interactions: click - selects that model id for the thread
ui.notes: The separators are U+00B7 with a space on each side, the ampersands are literal, and "1M" is that exact casing. This seed doubles as an equality sentinel for the registry, so any drift silently changes when the live catalog is fetched.

ui.element: Model row name and provider detail
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the model picker.
states: The row id is "<provider>/<id>", the name is the CLI's own name or the id, and the DETAIL line is the bare provider string
A reasoning model shows the seven thinking levels off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max and defaults to medium; a non-reasoning model shows no efforts at all, so the slider disappears
Rows are sorted by provider then name
An empty catalog is an error, not an empty list: "Pi listed no models."
interactions: click - selects the provider-slash-id, which the session splits into --provider and --model
ui.notes: A model id with NO slash cannot be passed to the CLI at all, so a catalog row whose provider or id is missing is skipped rather than shown.

ui.element: Model row collapsed from its effort variants
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the model picker.
states: One row per BASE slug: the CLI's -high, -medium and -low variants are collapsed and their efforts offered on the slider instead
The row's name has the matching " (High)", " (Medium)" or " (Low)" suffix stripped
Efforts are shown in the fixed order low, medium, high and default to high when available, otherwise the last available
When no row is current, the FIRST row is marked default so the picker always has one
No detail line is set at all for Antigravity rows
interactions: click - selects the base slug, which normalize may then pair with a forced effort
ui.notes: Selecting a model whose base slug contains "claude" suppresses --effort entirely, so the slider's value is silently ignored for those rows; and gpt-oss-120b is always forced to medium whatever the slider shows.

ui.element: Model row from the CLI's own initialize response
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the model picker.
states: The row id is the entry's "value", the name its "displayName" or that value, and the detail its "description"
The row whose value is exactly "default" is marked as the default row
A row whose supportsFastMode is true carries the fast tier "fast", which is what shows the Fast toggle
interactions: click - selects the model, which is sent mid-session as a set_model control request; the literal "default" is sent as JSON null
ui.notes: Claude's catalog arrives inside the session's own initialize response as well as from the static probe, and the probe's commands guard can destroy it entirely (PR-PROVCLI-026).

ui.element: The three quota window rows
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the usage panel.
states: Exactly three rows are possible, shown in this fixed order with these verbatim titles: "Premium requests", "Chat messages", "Code completions"
A row is absent when its snapshot is missing, null, explicitly unlimited, or has an entitlement that is not greater than zero
With all three absent the panel gets NOTHING at all for Copilot, because the reader returns nil rather than an empty set
ui.notes: The row ids are the snapshot KEYS (premium_interactions, chat, completions), not the titles. The percent can be NEGATIVE when the fallback branch is used with a negative usedRequests, which reaches the bar as-is.

ui.element: The two dollar-capped window rows
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the usage panel.
states: Exactly two rows are possible, in this order, with titles built as "<stem> · <formatted cap>": stem "5-hour limit" for the key fiveHour, and stem "Weekly" for the key weekly
The cap is rendered by ProviderCredits.money with the currency "USD" and the separator is space, U+00B7, space
A window whose cap is missing or not greater than zero is skipped
With no windows AND no plan name the panel gets nothing
ui.notes: These windows cap DOLLARS rather than requests, which is why the cap is in the title. On-demand credits are never throttled, which is why the rate-limit message points at them.

ui.element: Usage group rows and the AI credits row
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the usage panel.
states: Group rows are titled "<group name> · <bucket name>", with the group name defaulting to the literal "Models" and the bucket name to the literal "Limit"
The credits row is titled "AI credits · <n> remaining" and its bar is BINARY: 0 percent while any credits remain and 100 percent when none do
Antigravity never shows a plan name at all
ui.notes: The credits bar carries no proportion, so it reads as either empty or full; that is source behavior and is not a rendering bug.

ui.element: Window titles carrying a provider prefix or a limit name
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the usage panel.
states: Codex: the title is PlanLimitsReader.windowTitle for the window's duration, with " · <limitName>" appended ONLY when more than one snapshot was returned; the id is "<limitId or the literal codex>-<primary|secondary>"
Pi's Codex windows: the title is the literal "Codex · " followed by the window title for the duration in whole minutes, and the ids are exactly "codex-primary" and "codex-secondary"
Pi's plan name is the collected provider plan names joined by " · "
Codex with no windows still shows a row-less panel carrying the problem text "Codex reported no usage windows for this account."
ui.notes: Codex is the only provider in this area that surfaces a PROBLEM string in the usage panel; Copilot and Antigravity return nil and show nothing, and Command Code returns nil too.

ui.element: Sign-in state text for each CLI provider
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the Settings provider row.
states: Copilot: the GitHub login, with the suffix " · no Copilot access" appended when the account has no Copilot plan and the base defaulting to the literal "GitHub"; unreachable CLI reads as unknown, never signed out

Command Code: the name captured after "Authenticated as ", or the stored login's user name when the CLI says "authentication verified"; signed out on exit code 3 or on "not authenticated" or "not logged in"
Pi: the auth.json provider keys SORTED and joined by ", "; or signed in with NO name when a provider API key is in the environment
Antigravity: signed in with NO name, or signed out, or unknown - it never reports an account
ui.notes: The distinction between 'signed out' and 'unknown' is load-bearing: a Windows spawn failure must read as UNKNOWN, never as signed out, or the user is told to sign in when the real problem is that the CLI was not found.

ui.element: Compaction notices
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the notice row.
ui.colors: Not defined in this area; the level is .info for all of these.
states: Claude, Codex and Copilot all emit the identical verbatim "Context compacted."
Command Code emits "Compacting context." when it starts, and then either "Compacted context, freeing <n> tokens." with a group-formatted count or "Compacted context." when nothing was saved
Pi emits "Compacting the conversation…" with a horizontal ellipsis and no period, then "Conversation compacted" with NO trailing period
Copilot emits a WARNING with the server's error text instead when the compaction failed with one, and nothing at all when it failed without one
ui.notes: Six different strings for one concept, including two without trailing periods and one with an ellipsis. A porter normalizing them would change five user-visible strings at once.

ui.element: Provider-specific warning notices
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the notice row.
ui.colors: Not defined in this area; the level is .warning except where noted.
states: Claude usage limit: "Claude hit a usage limit." plus, when a reset time is known, " It resets at <formatted time>."
Codex MCP refusal: "Codex refused the MCP server configuration, so this session runs without MCP servers. Check MCP in Settings."
Codex retry: the error message, a space, then "Retrying."
Codex elicitation: "<server> asked for input, which Droppy Code cannot show yet." with the server defaulting to "An MCP server"
Copilot unsupported command: "/<name> opens a dialog that only Copilot's own terminal UI can show."
Command Code turn cap: "Command Code stopped at its cap of 400 round trips for one message. Send another to carry on."
Antigravity denied actions: "Antigravity held back <names> without prompting. Use Full access or add an allow rule in the CLI's settings."
Pi retry: the CLI's error text or the literal "Pi is retrying."
Pi extension error (level .error): the CLI's error text or the literal "Pi reported an extension error."
Pi notify: the CLI's message or the literal "Pi sent a notification.", at the level the CLI asked for
ui.notes: Two of these embed the product name on a user-visible surface; the rename decision governs them and they are not changed silently.

ui.element: Turn failure messages with no CLI text to show
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the failure row.
states: Claude: "Claude stopped before finishing." and, from the close path, "Claude exited."
Command Code: "Command Code stopped before finishing.", the nine exit-code messages, and "Command Code exited with code <status>."
Antigravity: "Antigravity stopped before finishing.", "Antigravity exited.", the held-back-permission failure and the sign-in hint
Pi: "Pi exited with status <status>" followed by a newline and the stderr tail when there is one
Copilot: "Copilot reported an error." and, on a 403 or a sign-in remediation, the appended " Check that your GitHub account has Copilot access, or sign in again with `copilot login`."
Codex: "Codex reported an error."
ui.notes: Several of these embed a shell command in backticks (`cmd login`, `copilot login`, `codex login`, `agy`) and two name a Settings path with U+2192 arrows. Whether those instructions are correct on Windows is a product question tied to UNK-0006, not something to reword from here.

ui.element: Fallback tool row titles when the call names no subject
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the tool row.
states: Claude: "Shell command", "Read file", "Write file", "Edit file", "Edit notebook", "Find files", "Search", "List files", "Fetch page", "Search the web", "Subagent", and "Skill · " with an empty tail
Copilot: "Shell command", "Read file", "Create file", "Edit file", "Search", "Find files", "Fetch page", "Search the web", "Subagent", "SQL query", "Create pull request", "Tool", and "Edit <n> files"

Command Code: "Shell command", "Monitor command", "Shell output", "Shell tasks", "Stop shell", "Read file", "List files", "Write file", "Edit file", "Find files", "Search", "Fetch page", "Search the web", "Sub-agent", "Agent output", and "Command · " with an empty tail

Codex: "Tool", "Web search", "Generate image", "Review", "Image", "Edit <n> files", "MCP", "tool", and the six collab verbs "Send out a head", "Brief a head", "Wait for heads", "Recall a head", "Resume a head", "List heads", with the default "Agent"
Pi: the literal "bash", the literal "." for a path-less ls, and otherwise the raw tool name
Antigravity: the humanized tool name, and "MCP" / "tool" for an unnamed MCP call
Every provider's MCP row reads "<server> · <tool>"
ui.notes: Note "Subagent" (Claude, Copilot) versus "Sub-agent" (Command Code) versus "Head" (Codex spawn) - three spellings for one idea, all verbatim. Note also that Command Code's humanize capitalizes only the first word while Antigravity's uses Swift's capitalized on the first word, which also lowercases its remaining characters; the two helpers must not be shared.

ui.element: Line-range details on a read row
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the tool row.
states: Copilot: "lines <first>–<second>" with an EN DASH, or "from line <first>" when the second value is negative; shown only for a two-element integer range
Command Code: "lines <offset>–<offset + limit>" with an EN DASH, shown only when BOTH offset and limit are integers
Antigravity: "L<start>–<end>" with an EN DASH when EndLine is greater than StartLine, else "L<start>"; shown only when a path was also found
Claude and Pi show no line range at all
ui.notes: Three different formats using the same U+2013 EN DASH. The dash is not a hyphen and not an em dash; substituting either changes three user-visible strings.

ui.element: Declined and blocked tool output text
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area; owned by the tool row.
ui.colors: Not defined in this area; the status .declined is what the row uses to pick its treatment.
states: Command Code decline, written into the reply file and echoed back by the CLI: "The user declined this in Droppy Code. Do not retry it; take another approach or explain what you would need."
Command Code mod default, when the reply carries no reason: "The user declined this in Droppy Code."
Command Code mod on an abort: "The turn was stopped."; on an orphan or the six-hour deadline: "Droppy Code did not answer."
Pi extension block reasons: "Final report: no tools", "Plan mode is read-only", and "The user declined this command" / "The user declined this file change" / "The user declined this tool call"
Command Code blocked-hook fallback: "Declined."; failed-tool fallback: "The tool failed."
Antigravity failed-tool fallback: "The tool failed."
ui.notes: Pi's three decline reasons are not merely display text: the app matches the shared prefix "The user declined this" to decide that a row reads declined rather than failed, so the extension's wording and the app's comparison must change together. Four of these strings embed the product name.

ui.element: Synthetic transcript placeholders that are deliberately NOT drawn
ui.geometry: Not defined in this area.
states: Claude Code writes its own bookkeeping under the model name "<synthetic>": "No response requested." for a turn it found unanswered when a session was resumed, and "(no content)" for an empty reply
Both are DROPPED and draw no chat row
A synthetic message that is flagged as an API error and whose text is neither placeholder IS drawn, as a warning notice rather than a message
ui.notes: Before this filter existed the chat drew "No response requested." as a reply from the lead. The two placeholder strings must be matched exactly, including the trailing period on the first and the parentheses on the second.
